title: Add props to outline schematic components and texts
description: Adds two props to SchematicViewer to outline rendered schematic components and texts with a dashed blue outline based on provided IDs.
body:
## What this does

Adds two props to `SchematicViewer`:

```tsx
<SchematicViewer
  circuitJson={circuitJson}
  highlightedSchematicComponentIds={["schematic_component_3"]}
  highlightedSchematicTextIds={["schematic_text_17"]}
/>
```

Each listed element that is rendered on the active sheet gets a dashed blue outline that follows pan, zoom and re-renders. Ids that are not rendered are ignored.

The use case is tscircuit.com's package Customize page (tscircuit/tscircuit.com#5810 and the stack above it), which outlines parts that were added or changed when a configuration is switched. It did that by inserting `<rect>`s into this viewer's SVG and watching it with a `MutationObserver`; with these props it only passes ids.

## How

- `SchematicElementHighlight` is an overlay positioned from the element's on-screen bounds, the same technique as the component hover outline
- That measurement logic existed twice, in `SchematicComponentMouseTarget` and `SchematicPortMouseTarget`. It now lives in `useSvgElementMeasurement` (with the port target's 4px padding as an option) and all three use it. The moved code is unchanged.

Because the overlay is re-measured on the next animation frame, the outline trails the schematic by a frame while panning, as the hover outline does.

## Checked

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run format:check` and `bun test` (59 pass, including the new `tests/highlighted-elements.test.tsx`)
- `examples/example40-highlighted-elements.fixture.tsx` in Cosmos: outlines appear and disappear with the checkboxes, realign after zoom and pan, and the component hover outline still works. Port outlines were not exercised by hand.
- A local build of this branch inside tscircuit.com: switching a configuration on the Customize page outlined the 3 added components and 5 notes, and the outlines cleared after 3 seconds

title: ci: alert when changes on main add more than 2 MB
description: Adds a size-growth rule to alert when a change lands on main and any measured size increases by more than 2 MB, with specific CI checks and Slack notifications for large increases.
body:
Adds one simple size-growth rule: **alert when a change lands on `main` and any measured size increases by more than 2 MB (2,000,000 bytes)**. Exactly 2 MB and smaller increases stay quiet. There are no percentage thresholds, and the same limit applies to every metric.

CI builds both revisions with their frozen dependencies and compares browser/worker bundles (raw and gzip), compressed/unpacked npm package sizes, and a clean production dependency installation. Measuring production dependencies catches additions such as `tsx`/`esbuild` even when the browser bundle stays unchanged. Reports and Slack messages show byte-size changes without percentages. The shared threshold is configured in `bundle-size.config.json`.

PRs get the `Bundle size budget` check and a comparison in the CI summary, with no Slack alerts or PR comments. Only completed pushes to `main` can send a Slack alert, including merges and direct automated dependency updates. Alerts link to the landed commit and full report. The trusted notification workflow has read-only repository permissions and uses only the existing `SLACK_AUTOMERGE_ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL` with its `MESSAGE` payload.

Validation:

- All 11 focused tests pass, including just below/exactly/one byte above 2 MB for every metric, independence from percentage growth, main-only notifications, the existing Slack Workflow payload, and HTTP failures. Slack requests are mocked.
- Both workflow files pass actionlint v1.7.7.
- Rechecked measurements from PR #6273's exact base (`afb44c0`) and head (`e33bd12`): production dependencies grew by **11.97 MB** (11.42 MiB), while browser and worker sizes stayed unchanged. The simplified check correctly exits 1. An unchanged-size comparison exits 0.

After merge, make **Bundle size budget** required in the `main` branch ruleset to block merges. Notifications become active once the workflow lands on the default branch. Push alerts report changes after landing; this PR does not change branch rules or gate the existing npm publishing workflow.

description: Add optional schematic_group.show_boundary, schematic_port.schematic_group_id, and schematic_port.boundary_position to define expanded subcircuit boundaries and public terminal geometry.
body:
An expanded subcircuit needs explicit boundary and public terminal geometry for converters.

Add optional `schematic_group.show_boundary`, `schematic_port.schematic_group_id`, and `schematic_port.boundary_position`. The port retains its existing `source_port_id`; `source_group_id` identifies its public interface owner. `center` is the external terminal, while `boundary_position` is its attachment to the expanded frame. Existing collapsed groups and component ports keep their representation.

Document coordinates, ownership, electrical connectivity and renderer behavior. The schema fixture uses actual core output from the real [CC2340R5 reference design](https://tscircuit.com/ShiboSoftwareDev/cc2340r5-reference-design/customize?package_release_id=bff7bbb1-c0df-4b3e-8cb2-5f5c706caa87&preview_file=dist%2Findex%2Fcircuit.json#schematic), release `bff7bbb1-c0df-4b3e-8cb2-5f5c706caa87`: the 27-component group, exported RESET_N terminal, and MCU physical reset pin. The core companion preserves all 16 original nets and adds eight GPIO nets for pins previously marked unconnected. Its proposed module has 13 wired public terminals: eight GPIOs plus supply, ground, reset and SWD.

Validation: 544 tests and TypeScript check pass. The schema implementation also passed build, Zod lint and snake-case checks.

Companions: [circuit-to-svg #932](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-to-svg/pull/932), [core #5445](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5445). Merge and publish schema → renderer → core; dependent proposals stay draft until their published dependency versions can be updated.

title: Add explosionview and assembly stage drawing props
description: Adds assembly drawing capabilities with explosion views and reusable stage definitions, enhancing the drawing functionality for parts and assemblies.
body:
Adds `assembly.drawing.explosionview` alongside `partview`, with reusable `stage` and `explosion` definitions, plus `partlabel` and `note`. Explosion views require `stageRef` and `explosionRef`; ordinary part views show assembled geometry and reject `explosionRef`. Both share viewport layout, section, hidden-edge and annotation controls. A drawing can reuse a populated-PCB stage or move a completed rotor as one unit while preserving assembled placement.

Selectors are trimmed nonempty arrays; physical offsets and paper coordinates accept distance strings and normalize to mm. Existing partRef-only views remain supported. The docs specify defaults, conflicts, output mapping, and the distinction from ordered `assembly.explosion.stage` playback.

Companion schema: https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/1003. Core selector resolution/emission is follow-up work; these are props contracts, not a claim that core already implements the new elements.

Pages accept `anchorAlignment`, reusing the board's nine-point enum (default: `center`). The selected corner, edge center or center defines (0, 0) for `paperX`/`paperY` and viewport centers, with +X right and +Y up. Labels and notes can instead select `xOffsetFromViewCenter`/`yOffsetFromViewCenter` per axis; conflicting or missing axes are rejected. Page-level relative notes select a same-page view with `viewRef`.

Validation: 781 tests pass, typecheck and build pass, formatting passes. All four required documentation generation scripts ran and generated changes are included. Renderer and all four fidget-counter visual snapshots: [circuit-json-to-drawing #10](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-drawing/pull/10).

title: docs: describe panel size limits as shaping the grid layout (#5067)
description: Updates documentation to clarify that panel size limits now shape the grid layout, allowing auto-sized panels to grow and grids to rearrange based on specified limits.
body:
Docs-only follow-up to #991, after Seve's review on https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5214 ("you want to change the panel layout algorithm, not just error").

Core#5214 now uses the panel size limits to shape a grid layout:

- When rows, columns and panel dimensions are left to the layout, a grid that would exceed `maxWidth` or `maxHeight` is rearranged into the smallest grid that fits.
- An auto-sized panel smaller than `minWidth` or `minHeight` grows to it, keeping its boards centred.
- Only limits that no layout can meet, or that explicit dimensions break, are reported.

The prop comments and `docs/panel-size-limits.md` / `docs/panel-manufacturing.md` said the limits were "validation only" and that panels are never resized; this updates them. No schema change. The README and generated overview are regenerated.

title: feat: place panel tabs with center offsets from board edges and a per-tab width (#5067)
description: Changes the paneltab component to use center offsets from board edges instead of a single offset, introducing new properties for better tab placement and width specification.
body:
Follows Seve's review on https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5208 ("paneltab needs a better api `centerOffsetFromBoardTopEdge`, `tabWidth`").

`<paneltab>` keeps a required `boardEdge` to pick the edge, and replaces `offset` with a center offset named after the board edge it is measured from (names from review):

```tsx
<paneltab boardName="B1" boardEdge="right" centerOffsetFromBoardTopEdge="6mm" />
<paneltab boardName="B1" boardEdge="top" centerOffsetFromBoardLeftEdge="12mm" tabWidth="3mm" />
```

- Left or right edge tabs use `centerOffsetFromBoardTopEdge` or `centerOffsetFromBoardBottomEdge`; top or bottom edge tabs use `centerOffsetFromBoardLeftEdge` or `centerOffsetFromBoardRightEdge`. Each is the distance from that board edge to the tab centre.
- Exactly one offset is required, and it must match `boardEdge`. Otherwise props reports, for example, "A left edge panel tab needs exactly one of centerOffsetFromBoardTopEdge or centerOffsetFromBoardBottomEdge" or "centerOffsetFromBoardTopEdge cannot place a tab on the top edge; use centerOffsetFromBoardLeftEdge or centerOffsetFromBoardRightEdge".
- New optional `tabWidth`: this tab's width along the board edge, a finite positive distance. It defaults to the panel's `tabLength`.

**Naming note:** on `<panel>`, `tabWidth` is the routed slot width and `tabLength` is the tab's span along the edge. Here `tabWidth` follows the review wording and means the tab's width along the edge. The doc comment says so explicitly.

**Breaking change:** `offset` is removed rather than deprecated. It was published in 0.0.724 (#988), but no Core release consumes `<paneltab>` yet; the Core implementation is still in review in core#5208.

`<paneltabkeepout>` and `tabCountPerEdge` are unchanged.

Validation: full props suite passes (779 tests, 20 assertions for this feature), typecheck and formatting pass, and all four documentation generators ran.

title: Align LED silkscreen bars with cathode pads
description: Fixes the alignment of LED silkscreen bars with cathode pads to ensure correct polarity representation in the PCB design.
body:
A two-pad LED with `cathodepin1` draws the silkscreen bar on the anode side even though the fabrication symbol and copper pads have the correct polarity. This occurs with the KT-0603R power LED on the [NEMA 23 controller](https://tscircuit.com/imrishabh18/nema-23-stepper-controller?version=1.4.27#pcb).

Use the same polarity resolver for the LED outline and fabrication symbol. For `led_p1.498mm_pw0.8mm_ph0.8mm_anodepin2_cathodepin1`, the bar moves to the left of pad 1. The default cathode-on-pad-2 orientation and pad geometry are preserved.

The regression covers both pin assignments and includes an SVG snapshot using the exact D_PWR footprint dimensions. I also rendered the LED through core before and after the fix and verified that pad 1 stayed at −0.749 mm while the silkscreen bar moved from +1.349 mm to −1.349 mm.

title: fix: keep board plane reservations independent of child groups
description: Fixes incorrect board plane reservations by ensuring that child groups do not influence the boards routing dimensions when their subcircuit IDs match.
body:
Board-level routing accidentally selects the first child PCB group sharing the board's subcircuit ID, then uses that group's dimensions for unbroken-plane reservations. A 30 × 20 mm board therefore exports an 8 × 6 mm plane when an ordinary 8 × 6 mm child group is present.

Stacked on #5437: `main ← repro/board-plane-reservation-bounds ← fix/board-plane-reservation-bounds`.

Use the existing `subcircuitIsBoard` distinction when inferring the routing group: a board no longer falls back to a child group merely because their subcircuit IDs match. An explicitly supplied `routingPcbGroupId` still selects that group, and non-board subcircuits retain the existing lookup. The production change is one condition plus its explanation, using the same board/group distinction already used for SRJ routing bounds.

The same native TSX repro now exports a 30 × 20 mm plane with and without the child group. Its snapshot changes only the incorrect reservation and its dimension caption. The explicit local-group control still receives 8 × 6 mm. There are no changes to copper, connectivity rules, routing algorithms, clearances, search budgets, dependencies, or board TSX.

Found on our four-motor USB-C/USB-PD STM32 motherboard. Comparing fresh first-callback captures with parent and fixed core changes both GND reservations from 20 × 20 mm at (0, 20) to the declared 174 × 99 mm at (0, 0). The non-plane SRJ content has an identical SHA-256 in both captures; the explicitly outlined DDR power reservation and overall board bounds also stay identical. These captures stop before the complete routing search; this does not claim the whole board routes.

This is independent of #5424 / #5426: those address redundant connection requests after actual copper pours exist. This fixes the plane description supplied before pour generation.

Validation:
- The corrected board-size assertion fails on parent code and passes with the fix; the before/after snapshots were rendered and visually inspected.
- Focused export, group, scope and plane tests: **23 passed, 1 failed**. The existing `breakout-fanout-props.test.tsx` snapshot differs by 0.08% on both parent and fix, with pixel-identical diff images. That unrelated snapshot is unchanged.
- Full TypeScript checking passes on repro and fix. Formatting and patch whitespace checks pass.
- Validation uses published capacity-autorouter 0.0.1080 and checks 0.0.276, matching current main's declared minimum versions.
- The full test suite was not run.

title: repro: child groups shrink board-level plane reservations
description: Fixes incorrect board-level plane reservations caused by child groups affecting autorouting output.
body:
A board-level unbroken ground plane is exported with the bounds of an unrelated ordinary child group. On a 30 × 20 mm board, adding an 8 × 6 mm group around R1 changes the router's plane reservation to 8 × 6 mm at the group position. The board, plane declaration, resistor positions and nets stay the same.

The TSX repro runs the normal native local router and captures its `autorouting:start` input before physical pours exist. Its two-panel snapshot draws the actual exported reservation in blue, the declared board in white, the child group in orange, and named GND terminals in yellow. It depicts routing input, not manufactured copper or fabricated routes. This branch deliberately records the incorrect output; stacked fix #5438 changes the assertion and snapshot to the board-sized reservation.

An explicit `routingPcbGroupId` control also checks that intentionally local routing still receives the group's bounds. There is no dogbone, saved routing, custom router callback, input mutation, added dependency, or config change in this repro. Only the TSX test and its SVG are added.

Found while building our four-motor USB-C/USB-PD STM32 motherboard. A fresh capture of that board's first autorouting callback confirms that both 174 × 99 mm GND reservations are exported as the 20 × 20 mm STM32 group at (0, 20). This is independent of #5424 / #5426, which concern connectivity after physical copper pours have been generated. This repro does not establish that fixing the reservation alone makes the entire motherboard route.

Validation: the new test and full TypeScript check pass. The corrected board-size assertion was also run against unchanged production code and fails with actual 8 × 6 versus expected 30 × 20.

title: fix: preserve copper-plane connectivity at breakout endpoints
description: Fixes copper-plane connectivity issues at breakout endpoints, preventing redundant routing requests in the autorouter.
body:
After native copper-pour generation, breakout endpoints already joined by that copper plane were exported as disconnected, making the native router request redundant routes. Core substituted the breakout point for its source pad, but the existing-copper export only recognized points carrying a `pcb_port_id`.

Stacked on #5424: `main ← repro/breakout-ground-plane-connectivity ← fix/breakout-ground-plane-connectivity`.

Extend the existing physical-copper graph to include breakout endpoints touching retained same-net copper on their own layer. Via-center endpoints are recognized through the actual via and its layer span, despite the center lying inside the drill hole. The SRJ export uses those physically connected point IDs. An endpoint does not inherit connectivity merely because its source pad touches a plane; the controls check missing escape copper and grounded source pads with disconnected endpoints. Router algorithms, search budgets and dependencies are unchanged.

The repro now uses the **complete imported STM32MP157DAB1 footprint from our four-motor USB-C/USB-PD motherboard: 354 pads and all 104 U70 GND assignments**. Native dogbone routing generates all 104 escape vias; a physical copper check confirms they touch one ground plane. The fix changes **103 redundant routing requests to 0**. No production-code adjustment was needed for the larger fixture.

The matching snapshot separates physical copper from requested connections. The complete chip, TOP escape close-up and INNER1 plane close-up are pixel-identical before and after the fix. A separate INNER3 request panel loses the dashed pink requests. The written pad → short trace → via → plane → via → short trace → pad path explains why those requests are redundant. Dashed lines are connection requests, not copper or prescribed track shapes.

The repro uses `routeRemaining={false}` to skip full-board routing and allow native pour generation, then exports that generated copper. This fix does not change the motherboard's first-pass routing input or resolve its initial iteration-limit failure, which occurs before physical pours exist. Initial plane-reservation bounds and reuse of existing vias during native plane routing are separate issues.

On the separate unchanged full-motherboard Circuit JSON capture taken after copper-pour generation, this fix also recognizes the affected U70.G6_VSS and U70.F7_VSS breakout endpoints as connected; the GND external-connectivity group grows from 532 to 657 points. This verifies export connectivity, not completion of full motherboard routing.

Validation:

- Updated full-STM32 repro passes, including the disconnected-endpoint controls. All three physical-copper panels were verified pixel-identical across the before/after snapshots. The existing copper-pour terminal-routing test passed in earlier verification.
- Full TypeScript check and changed-file formatting pass on both branches.
- Earlier broader verification: 9 copper-connectivity tests and 18 SRJ export/shared-capacitor handoff tests passed.
- Three existing dogbone snapshot tests failed identically on parent source and this fix: global handoff (0.14%), transforms/top-0 (0.10%), and solver events (0.21%). Those snapshots are unchanged.
- The previously investigated full-suite AM62L snapshot failure also exists on unchanged main ([repro log](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/43183539146/job/131065071153), [main log](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/43140285484/job/130925346524)). The full suite was not rerun locally for this fixture update.

body:
After native copper-pour generation, the STM32's ground pads already connect through their escape vias and a shared ground plane. Core loses that physical connection when exporting breakout endpoints, so the native router requests redundant connections.

This TSX repro uses **U70's complete STM32MP157DAB1 footprint from our four-motor USB-C/USB-PD motherboard**:

- All **104 motherboard GND assignments** are retained, with semantic ball names from the board.
- The same six-layer arrangement, 20 × 20 mm breakout region, native dogbone settings and relevant trace/via rules are used. The chip remains at its motherboard position, (0, 20).
- A 24 × 24 mm inspection board contains the chip and one native inner1 ground pour. Other nets, other motherboard components and unused 3D assets are omitted.

The test runs native dogbone routing → native ground-pour generation → core SRJ export → native point-pair generation. All 104 escape vias are generated afresh and checked geometrically against the same ground pour. **Expected: 0 new routes; actual: 103 redundant requests.** No patched solver, saved routes, injected copper or dependency/configuration changes.

The snapshot separates existing copper from connection requests. The complete chip, TOP escape close-up and INNER1 plane close-up are pixel-identical before and after the fix. A separate aligned INNER3 panel shows the actual native requests as dashed pink lines. The written path follows F7 pad → short trace → F7 via → shared INNER1 plane → G6 via → short trace → G6 pad. Pink dashes mean “connect these endpoints”; they are neither copper nor a prescribed track shape.

The test uses `routeRemaining={false}`: it skips full-board routing so native pour generation can complete, then tests the export of that existing copper. It does not reproduce or fix the motherboard's initial routing iteration-limit failure, which occurs before the physical pours are generated.

This defect was found when motherboard path search exhausted its budget on ground links before reaching DDR signals. The stacked fix is #5426; its matching full-STM32 snapshot changes **103 requests to 0**.

Rendered before/after images were compared and all three physical-copper panels are pixel-identical. The existing copper-pour terminal-routing test passed in earlier verification. title: fix: preserve authored pad layers in mixed-side footprints
description: Fixes the issue where an explicit component layer overwrites authored topbottom pad layers in mixed-side footprints, ensuring that pads without an explicit layer retain the component-layer default and preserving the correct pad layers during footprint flipping.
body: An explicit component `layer` currently overwrites authored top/bottom pad layers. Give explicit pad layers precedence and apply the existing footprint flip helper. Pads without an explicit layer retain the component-layer default. A real example is the [Amphenol 132289 edge-mount SMA](https://github.com/KiCad/kicad-footprints/blob/7ebfa6b23cc292a56f751b7b5f4a0e12eeef69dd/Connector_Coaxial.pretty/SMA_Amphenol_132289_EdgeMount.kicad_mod#L39), imported through the normal `kicad:` footprint-library path from an unmodified, pinned KiCad source. It has three front SMT pads and two back SMT pads. The old resolver incorrectly puts all five on one face; the fix preserves the contacts on both faces and swaps them when the connector is flipped. | Component | Placement | Top SMT pads | Bottom SMT pads | | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | | J1: Amphenol 132289 | top | 3 | 2 | | J2: Amphenol 132289 | bottom | 2 | 3 | | R1: ordinary 0402 | top | 2 | 0 | | R2: ordinary 0402 | bottom | 0 | 2 | The regression checks these counts, signal/ground port layers, and solder paste with subcircuit caching off and on. Cached and uncached pad positions, sizes, and layers must match exactly. A single three-pane snapshot shows the PCB, 3D top, and 3D bottom, including the actual [KiCad SMA STEP model](https://gitlab.com/kicad/libraries/kicad-packages3D/-/blob/77236890410eb655ba2e63e23f59a85cf45af290/Connector_Coaxial.3dshapes/SMA_Amphenol_132289_EdgeMount.step). The unmodified model is served locally during tests. Both PRs use identical component placement, camera positions, and panel layout, so the change shows the restored copper on each face. The original four-pad snapshot still shows the minimal color-only change. ![Fixed result: PCB, 3D top, 3D bottom](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/29f5ad48d25b2f855be28d0c6f838811ff6318df/tests/repros/__snapshots__/amphenol-132289-mixed-side-pad-layers.snap.svg) Pad `layer` values are authored relative to the footprint's `originalLayer`; component `layer` specifies placement. A bottom-authored footprint declares `originalLayer="bottom"` to avoid a second flip. The existing XIAO fixture now declares that metadata and retains its previous bottom-side snapshot. The new caching test exercises this convention through the actual Circuit JSON inflator. This work follows up on Jan Mrázek’s November 9, 2026 email to Severin Ibarluzea, titled *Re: mind.dump() "Interest in work with tscircuit (new venture-backed EDA tool)"*. Item 3 under “Placement” reported: > Setting layer on a component forces all of its pads onto that layer, so a mixed-side footprint loses its other-side pads. Validation: - Seven targeted tests pass, including the imported SMA, 0402 controls, cached geometry, and existing bottom-authored footprint cases. - All GitHub CI test shards, typecheck, build preview, formatting, class exports, and smoke checks pass for the updated three-pane snapshot. - TypeScript, Biome formatting, and `git diff --check` pass locally. - Both regressions are expected failures (`test.failing`) on the parent PR and normal passing tests on this PR. Snapshot comparisons run outside the expected-failure markers. Part 2 of [GitHub stack #5401](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/stack/5401), based on the regression/refactor PR #5399. title: feat: include per-connection compute cost in autorouting events
description: Expose per-connection solo search compute cost on autorouting events, allowing for detailed performance metrics during routing processes.
body:
Expose per-connection solo search compute cost on `autorouting:progress`, `autorouting:end`, and `autorouting:error`. Completion and failure read the autorouter directly, so stages that never emit progress still report their measurement. Local routing cache entries store and replay the same payload without changing the cache key. ### Contract Exported from `lib/events/index.ts`: ```ts type Iterations = number computeCostSummary: { metric: "hypergraph_route_search_iterations", measuredPairCount, // every pair measured, including ones cut from topPairs topPairs: [{ // highest first, at most 25 connectionName, rootConnectionNames, // every SRJ connection merged into this pair pcbPortIds, // measured endpoints; null for synthetic points iterations, // solo search iterations for this pair }], } ``` The three public events and the local progress event accept optional `computeCostSummary`. `GenericLocalAutorouter` accepts optional `getComputeCostSummary()`. The capacity mesh adapter duck-types the not-yet-released `getComputeCostSummary?.()` method from [tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3651](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3651), which builds on [tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph#315](https://github.com/tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph/pull/315). Both stepped and threaded progress attach the payload only when defined. No autorouter dependency or manifest change. ### Validation - `bunx tsc --noEmit` — passed. - `bunx bun@1.4.2 test tests/features/autorouting-compute-cost-*.test.tsx` — 4 passed, covering custom routers, completion/failure without progress, cache replay, both capacity mesh progress paths, and omission when the solver method is unavailable. - Related coverage command: ```sh bunx bun@1.4.2 test tests/features/autorouting-compute-cost-*.test.tsx tests/features/autoroutingphase-event-*.test.tsx tests/features/local-autorouting-phase-cache.test.tsx tests/features/autoroutingphase-emitted-paths-cache.test.tsx tests/features/autorouter-cache-provider.test.ts tests/features/async-local-cache-engine-cache-provider.test.ts tests/features/custom-autorouting-algorithmfn.test.tsx tests/utils/autorouting/capacity-mesh-autorouter ``` 21 passed, 1 failed: the existing `autoroutingphase-event-stage-index.test.tsx` PCB snapshot differs by 0.12%. The same command targeting that single test also fails with the same 0.12% difference in a clean archive of unchanged `main` (`02e53e3855eaaec48215c753d3bb00896365e662`) using the same installed dependencies. Its event assertions pass; the snapshot is unchanged in this PR. - The three requested regression cases failed on missing compute cost before the implementation, then passed. The committed cache test injects compute cost into an entry produced by the default router: custom algorithms explicitly bypass this cache, and the published solver does not provide the new method yet. - The installed Bun 1.3.14 rejects the threaded runtime; the commands above use Bun 1.4.2, matching test CI, without changing the global installation. ### Local-only unreleased autorouter check Built the local `ohmx/hypergraph-route-effort` autorouter at `df2df4bb0a3adfb9607c2445c856eb1017dcf466` with `bun run build`, temporarily linked its package, and ran `bunx bun@1.4.2 test ./.temp/rotated-resistor-compute-cost.test.tsx` (1 passed, 35 assertions). The TSX geometry is the autorouter's rotated-R2/tssop20 fixture, with `placementDrcChecksDisabled` because current core otherwise skips routing on its placement error. Both stepped and threaded renders reported `R2.pin2 → U1.pin2` first: 71 of 165 iterations across 22 measured pairs. Both second renders were cache hits and retained the measurement. The threaded first render emitted no progress, verifying terminal retrieval against the real solver. The stepped progress event also carried compute cost. The real check additionally verified that core wrote compute cost into the cache entry. Restored the published package afterward; neither linking nor the local test is committed. Naming: this is called `computeCostSummary` rather than "effort", because `effort` already names the autorouter effort setting on these same events. Review changes (from Seve): `share` dropped, metric renamed to `hypergraph_route_search_iterations`, and the payload is `computeCostSummary` everywhere (events, cache entry, CLI output). There is no stage total: a sum over every connection grows with board size, so it is not a useful score. The snapshot is frozen all the way down. ### How compute cost reaches the CLI ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant AR as autorouter pipeline 9 participant CM as core CapacityMeshAutorouter participant G as core Group stage participant CLI as cli AutorouterDiagnostics G->>CLI: autorouting:start G->>CM: start() Note over AR: solo pass runs while the port-point
stage is built, summary frozen once loop each progress tick, stepped or threaded CM->>AR: getComputeCostSummary() CM->>G: progress event with computeCostSummary G->>CLI: autorouting:progress (already spreads the event) end CM->>G: complete or error G->>CM: getComputeCostSummary() read directly, no tick needed G->>CLI: autorouting:end or autorouting:error with computeCostSummary CLI->>CLI: store under the stage key, include in debug output ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [2/2] Preserve unbroken inner copper planes in remote autorouting
description: Preserves unbroken inner copper planes in remote autorouting by ensuring that raw Circuit JSON requests maintain the intended copper pour intent during routing processes.
body:
Remote raw-Circuit-JSON requests lose `<copperpour unbroken>` intent because routing starts before copper pours render. Signal wires then cut through the intended reference plane.

Build SRJ from the live subcircuit tree and include it on raw solve/job requests when it contains an unbroken-plane reservation. Preserve the existing input format for requests without planes, and share the solve endpoint's request/result handling. Pass `allowViaInPad` as an optional converter parameter so it resolves the autorouter override before the board default, preserving explicit `false` values.

Fixes #3379.

### Stack

1. [#5374 — expected-failure reproduction and baseline snapshots](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5374), based on `main`.
2. **This fix**, based on `codex/repro-inner-plane-routing`.

Review and merge #5374 first, then restack this fix onto `main`. This PR removes `test.failing` from the reproduction and updates its two existing snapshots. It introduces **no new snapshot files**. One small assertion-only compatibility test checks ordinary pours in both HTTP modes.

### Before / after

| Plane intent lost | Plane intent preserved |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: signal cuts through inner1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/97e00512325a9c2bbdd60c5062155ac46e432dd8/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-inner-plane-remote-solve-pcb.snap.svg) | ![After: inner1 stays solid and inner2 carries the signal](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/7445776448bede0570fd3d7163a99c8022281e79/tests/repros/__snapshots__/repro-inner-plane-remote-solve-pcb.snap.svg) |

### Validation

- **16 focused tests pass**, covering explicit via-in-pad overrides, board defaults, nested board policy, remote input modes, ordinary pours, and both plane regressions.
- The expected-failure marker reports unexpected passes on the fixed behavior; these tests pass normally with the marker removed.
- Formatting and whitespace checks pass. No snapshot files are added relative to the repro branch.
- Current head `74457764`: all ten [GitHub test shards](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/42955874068), typecheck, formatting, dependency/class checks, package build/preview, and distribution smoke tests pass.

Remote servers must prefer the supplied `input_simple_route_json` for routing. Tests use real HTTP requests with the production solver in process; no live cloud service was used.

### Related work reviewed



- Reported plane-layer requirement: [tscircuit/tscircuit#5372](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5372); remaining remote transport gap: [core#3379](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/3379).
- Accepted API decision: [autorouter#2199](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2199#issuecomment-5381806016) closed the separate `routingLayers` design in favor of `unbroken` / `isCopperPour`. [props#808](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/808), [Circuit JSON#719](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/719), [core#3374](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3374), and [autorouter#2200](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2200) distinguish physical via fabrication policy from plane routing intent.
- Earlier remote fixes: [#3580](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3580), [#3744](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3744), [#4722](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4722), and open [#4884](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4884). This stack separates the visual reproduction from the fix and checks actual routed copper.
- Broader open API proposals: [core#5370](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5370) and [props#976](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/976). This stack uses the established API.
- Hard-keepout history: [#2221](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/2221), [#4014](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4014), [#4017](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4017), plus via-permission proposals [#4987](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4987), [#5008](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5008), [#5102](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5102), and [#5267](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5267). title: fix: emit the ordered path of every multi-port trace
description: Fixes the emission of ordered paths for every multi-port trace, ensuring that paths with 3 or more ports are correctly represented in the autorouting system.
body:
Stacked on the reproduction #5412. Routing also needs tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3708.

`path` is now emitted for every trace written with `path` and 3+ ports, not only for differential pair traces (#5384 made it conditional).

## Change (`lib/utils/autorouting/`)

- **`getSimpleRouteJsonFromCircuitJson.ts`**: drops the "is a pair member" condition from the ordered-path loop and drops the pair-only "both paths equal length" loop. Every ordered path keeps its own connection with `path`, as pair paths already did. That includes net-attached paths, which used to be merged into the net connection, so their order was lost. The renamed `explicitPath*` variables replace `differentialPairPath*`, because the set is no longer pair-only.
- **`net.X` semantics** (now documented in a comment): `path` lists ports only. A `net.X` entry attaches the chain to that net through the residual net connection (one representative point per chain, via the existing `reduceNetConnectionPointsForDifferentialPairPaths`). It is not a position in the chain.
- **`getDifferentialPairSourceTraceIds.ts`**: back to returning a `Set` (its pre-#5384 form). The pair tuples were only used by the removed loop.
- **`getDifferentialPairsForSimpleRouteJson.ts`**: a pair whose members have paths with different numbers of terminals is now rejected explicitly. It used to be rejected only because the conditional left the member without an SRJ connection.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
  subgraph before["Before"]
    T1["trace path C,A,B"] -->|"pair member?"| D1{yes}
    D1 -->|yes| P1["connection + path"]
    D1 -->|no| N1["connection without path, or merged into the net"]
  end
  subgraph after["After"]
    T2["trace path C,A,B (3+ ports)"] --> P2["connection + path [C, A, B]"]
    P2 -. "net.X entry" .-> N2["residual net connection joins at one point"]
  end
```

## Tests

- `trace-path-order.test.tsx`: changed from `test.failing` back to `test`.
  - "exports the written order of every trace path" **passes** (netless path, and path ending in `net.SIG` with a tap).
  - "routes a trace path in the written order" **fails in CI until `@tscircuit/capacity-autorouter` is bumped** to a release with #3708 (TODO in the test). Its snapshot is already the expected one, generated locally with that autorouter build linked: copper C–A, A–B (before: C–A, C–B).

## Existing tests updated (behavior change)

| Test | Before | After | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `autorouting-net-attached-trace-hint` | the only connection was the net's (`source_trace_id` undefined) | the only connection is the trace's, with a 3-port `path`; the trace hint is still in it | net-attached paths keep their own connection |
| `pmp23653-duplicate-connections-repro` | connection names = source net IDs | `netConnectionName` = source net IDs; still 2 connections, 18 endpoints, 16 traces | same reason; connection names are now `source_trace_*` |
| `differential-pair-branched-net-fallback` | threw "Could not find an SRJ connection … CK_P_TRUNK" | throws "members have paths with different numbers of terminals" | the old error depended on the conditional |

**Snapshot that will change when the autorouter is bumped:** `pmp23653-default-autorouter-duplicate-routing`. The trace is written `J5.pin1..6, J7.pin1..6, net.SECONDARY`. With ordered paths, the copper goes J5.pin6 → J7.pin1 as a long diagonal. Before, it used the shortest J5.pin1–J7.pin1 link. This is the written order, but it is a longer route.

## Local results

- Path/pair/SRJ-related set (140 files): 121 pass, 13 fail. 12 of the failures fail identically on `main` in my environment (small pixel diffs in pcb snapshots). The 13th is the expected routed-order test above.
- Same set with the #3708 autorouter build linked: `trace-path-order` passes. The only new change is the PMP23653 snapshot above.
- A net-attached path with a tap (linked build) routes C–A, A–B, TP–A with no errors.
- `tsc --noEmit` and `biome format`: clean.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: test: reproduce trace path order not emitted or routed
description: Reproduces a bug where trace paths are not emitted or routed in the correct order, specifically for paths involving multiple pins.
body:
Reproduction for "trace `path` should always be ordered, not conditionally". The fix is stacked on top of this PR.

`<trace path={["C.pin1", "A.pin1", "B.pin1"]} />` should be routed as the chain C → A → B. Today:

1. **SRJ:** `connections[].path` (added in #5384) is emitted only for traces referenced by a `<differentialpair>`. A plain path trace, or a path ending in `net.SIG`, has no `path`.
2. **Routing:** the copper follows the shortest tree, so it links C–A and C–B, never A–B.

```
exports the written order of every trace path
- [[pcb_port_4, pcb_port_0, pcb_port_2], [pcb_port_5, pcb_port_1, pcb_port_3]]
+ []

routes a trace path in the written order
-   "A-B",
+   "B-C",
```

Both tests are marked `test.failing` so CI stays green. The fix PR changes them back to `test`.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  subgraph written["Written: path C, A, B"]
    C1[C] --> A1[A] --> B1[B]
  end
  subgraph routed["Routed today"]
    C2[C] --- A2[A]
    C2 --- B2[B]
  end
```

The snapshot `tests/utils/autorouting/__snapshots__/trace-path-order-pcb.snap.svg` shows the routed copper going C–A and C–B.

Autorouter side: tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3707

title: Reproduce differential pair over nets not routing
description: Fixes autorouting failure when differential pairs are connected to nets that are not routed, leading to ratsnest lines and port-not-connected errors.
body:
## Reproduction A USB pair wired with nets, the way most users wire it: ```tsx const usb = { DP: "net.USB_DP", DM: "net.USB_DM" } ``` Nothing is routed. `getDifferentialPairSourceTraceOrThrow` treats `net.USB_DP` only as a trace name or port selector, so it throws. The throw happens inside the async autorouting effect. It is logged to the console, not recorded in circuit JSON, so the board just has ratsnest lines and port-not-connected errors. ```mermaid flowchart LR A["positiveConnection = 'net.USB_DP'"] --> B{"Trace named
'net.USB_DP'?"} B -- no --> C{"Port matching
'net.USB_DP'?"} C -- no --> D["throw: Could not find source trace"] D --> E["Async autorouting effect dies
(console only, not in circuit JSON)"] E --> F["No copper: ratsnest +
port-not-connected errors"] ``` The snapshot draws the ratsnest and error overlay so the failure is visible. The test asserts the current buggy state (`pcb_trace` is empty). The fix PR (#5381) flips it. ```sh bun test tests/repros/repro-differential-pair-net-connection ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: [1/2] Reproduce remote routing through an unbroken inner plane
description: Reproduces a bug where raw remote solve and job requests lose copperpour unbroken intent before copper pours render, affecting signal routing on inner planes.
body:
Raw remote solve and job requests lose `<copperpour unbroken>` intent before copper pours render. On this four-layer fixture, the signal cuts through inner1 instead of preserving the intended reference plane.

This is **part 1 of the stack**: `main` → [#5374 reproduction](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5374) → [#5375 fix](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5375). Both PRs are ready for review; this PR contains no production changes.

### Reproduction

- Two labeled PCB SVGs capture the defect using the real default autorouter behind local HTTP solve/job endpoints. All snapshot files are introduced here.
- Both cases use Bun's `test.failing()` with the intended contract: no signal wires on inner1, routing on inner2, and an inner1 plane reservation in the router input.
- Rendering, snapshot comparisons, trace creation, and full-stack via checks run in `beforeAll`, outside the expected-failure body. Setup or snapshot regressions fail CI normally.
- The fix removes `.failing` and retains the same intended-behavior assertions.

### Validation

- Both expected-failure cases execute and pass as expected on the baseline.
- Verified that the same marked tests fail with Bun's unexpected-pass error on fixed production code; normal `test()` passes there.
- Existing baseline snapshots are unchanged. Scoped formatting and whitespace checks pass.
- Current head `97e00512`: all ten [GitHub test shards](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/actions/runs/42851511692), typecheck, formatting, dependency/class checks, package build/preview, and distribution smoke tests pass.

### Related work reviewed



- Reported plane-layer requirement: [tscircuit/tscircuit#5372](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit/issues/5372); remaining remote transport gap: [core#3379](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/3379).
- Accepted API decision: [autorouter#2199](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2199#issuecomment-5381806016) closed the separate `routingLayers` design in favor of `unbroken` / `isCopperPour`. [props#808](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/808), [Circuit JSON#719](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/719), [core#3374](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3374), and [autorouter#2200](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/2200) distinguish physical via fabrication policy from plane routing intent.
- Earlier remote fixes: [#3580](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3580), [#3744](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/3744), [#4722](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4722), and open [#4884](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4884). This stack separates the visual reproduction from the fix and checks actual routed copper.
- Broader open API proposals: [core#5370](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5370) and [props#976](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/976). This stack uses the established API.
- Hard-keepout history: [#2221](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/2221), [#4014](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4014), [#4017](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4017), plus via-permission proposals [#4987](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4987), [#5008](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5008), [#5102](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5102), and [#5267](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5267). Plane reservations retain their separate semantics.

title: Fix named-net routing via a phase-selected pin
description: Fixes autorouting failure when a phase-selected pin does not route a named net connection, resulting in zero routed traces on the PCB.
body:
Route a named net when an `<autoroutingphase>` selects one of its pins. In the repro, `U1.pin8` connects to `DATA`, `U2.pin1` connects to `DATA_ALIAS`, and the two nets are tied. The `DATA_ONLY` phase selects `U2.pin1`. With `routeRemaining={false}`, the phase never started and the board had **zero routed traces**.

The phase planner selected the pin-to-net trace but left the net connection that the router uses outside the phase. It now adds the nets that share the selected single-port trace’s connectivity key to the same phase. This includes tied names such as `DATA_ALIAS`.

The regression verifies that `DATA_ONLY` starts exactly once and produces **one PCB trace from `U1.pin8` to `U2.pin1`**. The unrelated `LATER` net stays deferred. The assertions live in [repro #5342](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5342) and are enabled here.

| Repro · no routed trace | Fix · DATA pins connected |
| --- | --- |
| ![PCB before the fix, with no trace between the DATA pins](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/011ff4171850988931f136a2422ed375bb75703f/tests/repros/__snapshots__/phase-net-pcb.snap.svg) | ![PCB after the fix, with U1 pin 8 routed to U2 pin 1](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/core/4b8ac056153f7d0b14087b74558eb7c79e8d4cc3/tests/repros/__snapshots__/phase-net-pcb.snap.svg) |

Run `bun test tests/repros/phase-net.test.tsx`.

title: Fix plated-hole solder paste ownership
description: Fixes the ownership assignment for solder paste records associated with circular plated holes in KiCad exports, ensuring correct PCB component IDs are applied.
body:
**Export a board with one connector, `J1`, containing one SMT pad and one circular plated hole.** In the repro, the KiCad export contains three footprints. `J1` holds the connector pads. Each of two unnamed footprints holds one circular paste aperture, one on `F.Paste` and one on `B.Paste`.

Core created the `pcb_solder_paste` records without the hole’s `pcb_component_id`, so the exporter treated them as standalone items. `PlatedHole` now copies that ID onto both paste records when it generates them for circular, pill-shaped and oval holes.

The regression renders a circular plated hole both directly and through a cached subcircuit. In both cases it checks the owner IDs in Circuit JSON and verifies that KiCad exports **one footprint, `J1`, containing both `F.Paste` and `B.Paste`**. The assertions were introduced as `test.failing` in [repro #5340](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5340) and are enabled here.

Run `bun test tests/repros/paste-owner.test.tsx` to check both exports. [Circuit JSON ownership and KiCad footprint assertions](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/4d6dc8189b42ff1b6b160f66b2443ea3e71fcb71/tests/repros/paste-owner.test.tsx)

title: Use the board via-to-pad clearance for routing DRC
description: Adjusts routing DRC to utilize board-specific via-to-pad clearance values for accurate gap measurements.
body:
## Motivation

A board can specify different copper clearances for via-to-pad and pad-to-pad pairs. Designers need routing DRC to apply the rule for the copper pair it is measuring.

## Actual behavior

On `main`, a via sits 0.14 mm from an unconnected top-side pad. Running the routing checks on that same geometry produces these results:

| Board via-to-pad minimum | Board pad-to-pad minimum | Actual on main | Expected |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.20 mm | 0.10 mm | No violation | Report the 0.14 mm gap against 0.20 mm |
| 0.10 mm | 0.20 mm | One violation | Accept the 0.14 mm gap |

## Expected behavior

Use the board's `min_via_edge_to_pad_edge_clearance` for via-to-pad checks, including when it is explicitly zero. If the board omits it, fall back to the pad-to-pad minimum and then the existing manufacturing default. An explicit `minClearance` passed by a caller still takes precedence.

## Verification

Both cases in the table failed on `main` and pass with this change. The regression test exercises `runAllRoutingChecks` and checks the pair IDs, measured gap and required minimum. The PCB snapshot shows the diagnostic for the first row.

![PCB diagnostic showing the 0.14 mm gap against a 0.20 mm minimum](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/techmannih/checks/4be821828f17304e6a8acf7eb69045287144c6ff/tests/lib/__snapshots__/via-pad-board-clearance.snap.svg)

`bun test` passed all 789 tests. TypeScript and formatting checks also passed.

title: Repro: cutout flush with the board edge is emitted as a separate Edge.Cuts loop
description: Fixes a bug where a cutout that runs flush with the board edge is incorrectly emitted as a separate Edge.Cuts loop instead of being merged into the board outline.
body:
## What

Adds a repro test with a snapshot for an Edge.Cuts bug: a `pcb_cutout` that runs to the board edge and ends **exactly on it** (flush, not past it) is emitted as its own closed loop instead of being merged into the board outline.

## Snapshot (current behaviour on `main`, v0.0.122)

A board with a breakaway tab held by two mouse-bite bridges, rendered with pcb-stackup like the other gerber snapshots. The two side slots run to the bottom board edge.

<img src="``https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/blob/145e4c4a7a198dcf6bce475c28caefe428bae32e/tests/gerber/__snapshots__/edge-flush-cutout-top.snap.svg?raw=true"`` width="700" alt="Breakaway tab board with the two side slots marked in red" />

The red areas are the bug: each side slot is a standalone closed Edge.Cuts loop sitting on top of the board edge, instead of being part of the board outline.

The red marking is added by the test. pcb-stackup fills the outline layer with the even-odd rule, so by itself it draws such a loop as an open slot and the render looks the same with and without the bug.

## Why it matters

Physically such a cutout is a notch in the board outline. Emitted as a standalone loop it shares a segment with the outer contour. JLCPCB's Gerber viewer reads that area as solid board, so a breakaway slot drawn this way is not shown as a cut.

Seen on a real board: two 2.25 mm slots from the bottom edge (a breakaway tab) came out as separate loops lying on the board's bottom edge, and the viewer rendered the tab as solid.

## Repro

`tests/gerber/generate-gerber-with-edge-flush-cutout-repro.test.ts`

- 40 × 30 mm board with pads, traces and silkscreen
- two polygon cutouts from the bottom edge (`y = -15`) up to the tab's bridges, flush with the edge
- one cutout between the bridges, fully inside the board (must stay a separate loop)
- six 0.4 mm mouse-bite holes

The test passes on this branch; its snapshot records the buggy output. The fix is stacked on top and updates the snapshot: [tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber#246](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gerber/pull/246).

## Cause

`doesSolidCutoutOverlapBoardEdge` only returns true when the cutout extends *outside* the board outline. A cutout that stops exactly on the edge has nothing outside the board, so it is classified as internal.

title: Outline changed schematic parts through schematic-viewer props (9/9)
description: Draws dashed outlines around changed schematic parts on the Customize and reference-design pages for three seconds using the schematic viewers new props.
body:
Part 9 of 9 of the stack that splits #5781 (by ShiboSoftwareDev). Targets the branch of #5815.

## What this does

Draws the change outlines on the Customize and reference-design pages again, now through the schematic viewer instead of by editing its SVG:

- The schematic view passes `changes.schematicComponentIds` and `changes.schematicTextIds` (from part 3, #5810) to the viewer's `highlightedSchematicComponentIds` / `highlightedSchematicTextIds` props, added in tscircuit/schematic-viewer#312
- `@tscircuit/schematic-viewer` goes from `^2.0.108` to `^2.0.110`, the first release with those props

After a configuration switch, parts and notes that were added or changed get a dashed outline in the schematic for three seconds. There is no PCB highlighting.

## Effect on existing pages

- The props are `undefined` wherever no changes provider is mounted, which is every page except Customize and reference designs, so no outlines are drawn there
- The viewer bump applies to every schematic view on the site. Besides the new props it brings 2.0.109 ("Fit schematics to the selected sheet frame", tscircuit/schematic-viewer#308) and moves the viewer's own `circuit-to-svg` from 0.0.432 to 0.0.445.

## Checked

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run lint` and `bun test` pass on this branch
- Local dev server against the production API on this branch, with the published 2.0.110: turning "External LF crystal" off and on again on the Customize page outlined the 3 re-added components and 5 notes, and the outlines cleared after 3 seconds. Turning a part off draws nothing, since only additions and changes are reported.

title: Track schematic changes between package configurations (3/8)
description: Adds change tracking between two circuits, allowing the Customize page to identify which schematic parts a configuration switch added or changed.
body:
Part 3 of 8, splitting #5781 (by ShiboSoftwareDev) into a stack.

## What this does

Adds change tracking between two circuits, so the Customize page can tell which schematic parts a configuration switch added or changed:

- `getPackageCircuitChanges` compares two Circuit JSON arrays by authored content (group path + name) and returns `schematicComponentIds` and `schematicTextIds`. It compares source and schematic fields only and ignores generated ids, so a PCB-only difference is not a change.
- `PackagePreviewChangesProvider` remembers the previous circuit for a selection and exposes the changes for three seconds
- Under that provider, the schematic view hands the viewer a fresh array with a bumped `editCount`, so value-only configuration changes re-render

Nothing is drawn in this PR. Compared with #5781:

- PCB change highlighting is removed. The PCB view is not touched by this PR any more.
- The hook that drew schematic outlines by inserting rectangles into the viewer's SVG (`use-schematic-change-highlights.ts`, with a `MutationObserver`) is removed. Outlines will come from new `highlightedSchematicComponentIds` / `highlightedSchematicTextIds` props on `@tscircuit/schematic-viewer`, wired up in a part 9 once a viewer release has them.

## Effect on existing pages

None intended. Nothing mounts the provider in this PR. Without it `usePackagePreviewChanges()` is `null` and the schematic view hands the viewer the same circuit array instance as before.

title: Let package preview hooks read identity from an optional scope (2/8)
description: Adds PackagePreviewScope, an optional context that supplies the release, preview file, circuit JSON and GLB for an embedded preview, allowing hooks to resolve identity without a provider.
body:
Part 2 of 8, splitting #5781 (by ShiboSoftwareDev) into a stack.

## What this does

Adds `PackagePreviewScope`, an optional context that supplies the release, preview file, circuit JSON and GLB for an embedded preview. The hooks and viewer that read `useParams()` / `useUrlParams()` directly now call `usePackagePreviewIdentity()`, which returns exactly those route and query values when no provider is mounted.

- `useCurrentPackageRelease`, `useCurrentPackageCircuitJson` and the 3D view resolve identity through the new hook
- `usePackageRelease` / `useCurrentPackageRelease` accept an optional `refetchOnMount`
- With a scope, `useCurrentPackageCircuitJson` returns the scoped circuit without fetching, and the 3D view renders the scoped GLB

## Effect on existing pages

None intended. No provider is mounted anywhere in this PR, so every caller takes the route/query path it took before. Existing callers pass no `refetchOnMount`; react-query 3 treats `undefined` the same as its default (`shouldFetchOn` only special-cases `false` and `"always"`), and the app's `QueryClient` sets no default options.

This is the PR to read most carefully: `useCurrentPackageRelease` is used across the package page, sidebar, settings and releases.

## Checked

title: Load gzip-compressed Circuit JSON preview files (1/8)
description: Adds support for loading gzip-compressed Circuit JSON preview files, allowing package pages to preview large circuits efficiently.
body:
Part 1 of 8, splitting #5781 (by ShiboSoftwareDev) into a stack. Base: `main`.

## What this does

Package builds can publish large circuits as `circuit.json.gz`. This lets the package page preview them.

- `getPreviewCircuitFiles` also matches `circuit.json.gz` and `*.circuit.json.gz`
- `useCurrentPackageCircuitJson` downloads a selected `.gz` file through `/package_files/download` and decompresses it in the browser instead of reading `content_text`. It also returns `packageFiles`.
- `fetchPackageArtifact` retries once when the CDN serves a 404 that was cached while a new artifact was still publishing
- The "N Builds" selector is hidden when a release has `dist/preview.json`

## Effect on existing pages

- Packages with no `.gz` circuit files and no `dist/preview.json`: no change. Uncompressed preview files still load through `/package_files/get`.
- Packages that already publish `*.circuit.json.gz`: those files now count as preview files and open with `?preview_file=`.
- Packages with `dist/preview.json` (today `ShiboSoftwareDev/cc2340r5-reference-design`, which has 64 state files): the selector is hidden so the states are not listed as builds.

## Checked

- `bunx tsc --noEmit`, `bun run lint` and `bun test` pass on this branch
- Local dev server against the production API, at part 3 of the stack (parts 1-3 together): an ordinary package (`seveibar/usb-c-flashlight`) renders schematic, PCB and 3D as before; the demo package loads `?preview_file=dist/index/states/<id>/circuit.json.gz` and shows no Builds selector

Merge bottom-up. Each part builds, typechecks and passes tests on its own, so the stack can stop after any of them.

title: Add a safe search-index-only rebuild action
description: Adds a manual GitHub Action to rebuild only the search index, without changing the component catalogue or stock.
body:
Adds a manual GitHub Action to rebuild only the search index, without changing the component catalogue or stock.
It uses small batches, retries temporary failures, and verifies the rebuilt index before enabling it.

title: Fix JSON output after D1 stock-sync retries
description: Fixes JSON output handling in stock-sync job by separating successful and failed JSON attempts, ensuring valid JSON is returned to the stock job.
body:
A stock-sync job can fail even after a database request succeeds on retry. `retry-command.sh` reruns failed commands after a delay, but it combines the failed attempt's JSON error with the successful attempt's JSON data. The stock job cannot read that combined output as valid JSON.

This change captures each JSON attempt separately, sends failed attempts to the error log, and returns only the successful JSON to the stock job. If every attempt fails, the script reports the final failure.

title: Reduce D1 load by caching table filter options
description: Caches dropdown values for resistor and capacitor pages to reduce load by skipping dropdown queries for JSON requests and caching HTML dropdown values for 15 minutes.
body:
Resistor, capacitor, and other pages using the shared table handler recalculate dropdown values for each uncached search. These queries scan large tables, even for JSON requests that do not use the dropdowns.

This change skips dropdown queries for JSON and caches the HTML dropdown values by component type for 15 minutes. Existing catalog-sync cache purges and explicit cache refreshes also clear these values.

title: Add Buzzers category with filters and JSON API
description: Adds a Buzzers link on the home page and buzzerslist with package, Basic, and Preferred filters, and exposes the same results through the API at buzzerslist.json.

Imports parts classified as `Buzzers` across the catalog's parent-category renames, preserving prices, stock, assembly flags, and attributes. Includes the D1 table migration, indexes, type definitions, and sync registration; adds `buzzer` to the default derived-table build so data is populated after merge.

title: Expose JLCPCB's Standard-only mark on verified parts
description: Adds is_standard_only to the verified component that exact-part lookups return, indicating whether a part is marked as Standard only by JLCPCB, which affects the assembly service selection for PCBA.
body:
## Summary

Adds `is_standard_only` to the verified component that exact-part lookups return (`/api/search?q=C…`).

JLCPCB marks some parts "Standard only": its Economic PCBA service cannot place them, so a single one moves the whole board to Standard PCBA (higher setup and stencil fees, a loading fee on every part). Typical cases are parts smaller than 0402, many ESP32 modules, 5050 addressable LEDs and some very small DFN/LGA/CSP chips, but it varies part by part, so it cannot be inferred from the package. `circuit-json-to-jlcpcb-quote` needs the mark to quote the right assembly service.

## Change

- `fetchExactStock` reads JLCPCB's `componentProductType` from the record it already fetches: `2` means Standard only, `0` means either service can place it.
- `is_standard_only` is `true`, `false`, or `null` when JLCPCB's record has no such field. Null means unknown, not economic-capable.
- No schema change: the verified component is stored as JSON. Parts verified before this change simply lack the field until their next refresh.

## How the mapping was checked

- All 73 parts of a board JLCPCB quoted as Economic PCBA have `componentProductType: 0`.
- Five known Standard-only parts have `2`: ESP32-WROOM-32-N4 (C82899), ESP32-WROOM-32E-N4 (C701341), ESP32-S3-WROOM-1-N16R8 (C2913202), WS2812B-B/T (C2761795), WS2812C (C114587).
- On a second board, the 11 parts with `2` are nine 0201 passives, a 0.8x0.6mm DFN-3 transistor and a 2x2mm LGA-12 accelerometer.

I have not seen any other value of `componentProductType`; anything that is not `2` is reported as `false`.

## Testing

- `bun test tests/requested-stock.test.ts`: new test for `2`, `0` and a missing field.
- `cf-proxy` `vitest run requested-stock`: the stored field is served through `/api/search`.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit --project cf-proxy/tsconfig.json` passes.

---

title: Update schematic-symbols to 0.0.251 as a runtime dependency
description: Moves schematic-symbols from devDependencies at 0.0.237 to runtime dependencies at 0.0.251 to ensure consumers receive the corrected dependency for four-pin crystal previews, fixing detached wires and overlapping labels.
body:
Four-pin crystal previews can use old artwork against the newer pin positions generated by core, leaving wires detached and labels overlapping.

Move `schematic-symbols` from `devDependencies` at `^0.0.237` to runtime `dependencies` at `^0.0.251`. Runframe's library build externalizes symbols, so a development-only update does not supply the corrected dependency to consumers. Core already adopted this version in https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/4966.

Before, the website dependency reproduction resolves symbols `0.0.239`; with this manifest it resolves `0.0.251` without a website override, and the crystal terminals align.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Detached crystal wires](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/tscircuit.com/ecce808b4edc7c7dda0ea8b73a47a21370f4a037/website-crystal-before.png) | ![Aligned crystal terminals](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/tscircuit.com/ecce808b4edc7c7dda0ea8b73a47a21370f4a037/website-crystal-after.png) |

These images use the same Circuit JSON and website-resolved schematic renderer with the old/new symbol versions; they are not captures of a rebuilt Runframe.

Validation:
- Isolated before/after package-manifest tarballs resolved against the original website lockfile using Bun: `0.0.239 → 0.0.251`, with no website symbol override.
- Existing renderer reproduction: all four terminal positions match with `0.0.251`; focused Vite renderer bundle also verified.
- `git diff --check` and `npm pack --dry-run --ignore-scripts` pass. Full Runframe builds and test suite have not been run locally (about 1.5 GB disk space remaining); CI validation is pending.

Only `package.json` changes; Runframe disables lockfile saving. Related: https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit.com/pull/5805.

title: Collapse repeated build errors and print a count per error type
description: Only the first 10 errors (and warnings) of each type are logged; the rest are reported as a count, improving clarity in build error reporting.
body:
## Problem

`tsci build` prints every circuit JSON error on its own line. A board that fails early repeats one diagnostic hundreds of times and buries the few distinct causes; agents using the CLI were writing scripts just to count error types.

## Change

- Only the first 10 errors (and warnings) of each type are logged; the rest are reported as a count.
- Every error is written to `dist/<entry>/errors.json` next to `circuit.json`, and the summary names that path. A build without errors removes the file, so a stale list is never left behind.
- Errors are followed by a per-type total.
- Applies to both the single-process and `--concurrency` worker paths. The worker result still carries every message.

```
Port [U1.pin10] is not connected to net [N10] by a PCB trace.
… 15 more pcb_port_not_connected_error not shown
27 error(s), all written to dist/board/errors.json:
  25  pcb_port_not_connected_error
   1  pcb_autorouting_error
   1  source_trace_not_connected_error
```

Builds with 10 or fewer errors per type only gain the per-type total and the file. Exit codes are unchanged.

title: feat: capture per-connection compute cost in autorouter diagnostics
description: Captures optional per-connection compute cost from autorouter progress, end, and error events in the existing CLI diagnostics, preserving the single-active-phase design and enhancing diagnostic output.
body:
Captures optional per-connection compute cost from autorouter progress, end, and error events in the existing CLI diagnostics. Compute cost stays separate for each subcircuit and actual routing-stage order, with the existing computed phase ordinal as the fallback, while preserving the single-active-phase design. Terminal payloads override progress measurements. - Adds metric, totals, pair provenance, endpoint labels, and iterations to `board.meta.json` phase entries and cooperative timeout artifacts. - Resolves PCB endpoints through source ports and component names, falling back to the connection name for missing or synthetic endpoints. Prints the top five pairs on diagnostic errors and successful debug runs. - Preserves compute cost from interleaved sibling terminal events even when the existing active phase belongs to another sibling. Preparation errors without a known stage remain unscoped. - A malformed compute cost summary only prints a warning. Adds no flag, dependency bump, or always-on report file, and leaves existing debug artifact writing unchanged. - The pure labeling and formatting helpers live in `lib/shared/compute-cost-summary.ts`. The diagnostics class keeps a small set of named steps: `rememberComputeCost`, `getLabeledComputeCost`, `reportComputeCost`, and `recordUntrackedStage` (for a sibling subcircuit routing at the same time, or an error before any start). The code went through two rounds of readability review. This consumes optional fields from an **unreleased core change**, whose PR is being opened in parallel. The producer side is tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3651 and tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph#315. The CLI uses each project's installed tscircuit, so events without `computeCostSummary` remain supported indefinitely. Validation: ```sh bunx tsc --noEmit bun test tests/shared/autorouter-diagnostics.test.ts tests/shared/autorouter-diagnostics-compute-cost-*.test.ts tests/shared/dev-server-autorouter-debug.test.ts bunx biome format lib/shared/autorouter-diagnostics.ts tests/fixtures/get-compute-cost-test-fixture.tsx tests/shared/autorouter-diagnostics-compute-cost-*.test.ts git diff --check ``` Typecheck passed; 19 tests passed with 0 failures (`bun test tests/shared/autorouter-diagnostics.test.ts tests/shared/autorouter-diagnostics-compute-cost-*.test.ts`); formatting checks passed. The compute cost tests emit simulated events through a fake root backed by circuit JSON from a real TSX board. The chain from a real autorouter build through core to this class was also run locally on a rotated-resistor board: `R2.pin2 -> U1.pin2 (71 iters)` came out first. Dev-server formatting is unchanged: its formatter does not have the circuit JSON lookup needed for endpoint labels, and the design scopes v1 to Node rendering. Naming: this is called `computeCostSummary` rather than "effort", because `effort` already names the autorouter effort setting on these same events. Review changes (from Seve): `share` dropped, metric renamed to `hypergraph_route_search_iterations`, and the payload is `computeCostSummary` everywhere (events, cache entry, CLI output). There is no stage total: a sum over every connection grows with board size, so it is not a useful score. The snapshot is frozen all the way down. ### How compute cost reaches the CLI ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant AR as autorouter pipeline 9 participant CM as core CapacityMeshAutorouter participant G as core Group stage participant CLI as cli AutorouterDiagnostics G->>CLI: autorouting:start G->>CM: start() Note over AR: solo pass runs while the port-point
stage is built, summary frozen once loop each progress tick, stepped or threaded CM->>AR: getComputeCostSummary() CM->>G: progress event with computeCostSummary G->>CLI: autorouting:progress (already spreads the event) end CM->>G: complete or error G->>CM: getComputeCostSummary() read directly, no tick needed G->>CLI: autorouting:end or autorouting:error with computeCostSummary CLI->>CLI: store under the stage key, include in debug output ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Fix autorouter worker count in tsci build
description: Fixes the issue where the tsci build command rejected the --autorouter-threads option, allowing it to accept a positive integer to specify the number of solver workers for local autorouters.
body:
`tsci build` previously rejected `--autorouter-threads` as an unknown option. The flag now accepts a positive integer and overrides the project’s `platformConfig.autorouterThreads` for supported local autorouters. A value of `1` runs the solver inline.

```sh
tsci build --concurrency 3 --autorouter-threads 2
```

This builds up to three circuit files concurrently and requests two solver workers per circuit.

The integration test runs this command on three circuit files with a project default of one solver worker. It verifies that all three `RootCircuit` instances receive `2`. Parser tests also cover zero, negative, fractional, and nonnumeric counts.

Stacked on [#5749](https://github.com/tscircuit/cli/pull/5749), which reproduces the original CLI error.

title: Document remaining-routing preflight and its 50-connection threshold
description: Updates documentation to clarify the behavior of the routeRemaining setting in relation to the implicit routing phase and the 50-connection threshold.
body:
The board reference previously described omitting `routeRemaining` and explicitly setting it to `true` as equivalent. Under the default preflight, the implicit routing phase runs only when **50 or fewer connections remain** after explicit phases finish.

| Board configuration | What core does |
|---|---|
| 50 remaining, `routeRemaining` omitted | Routes all 50. |
| 51 remaining, `routeRemaining` omitted | Skips the entire implicit phase and reports a routing error. |
| 51 remaining, `routeRemaining={true}` | Routes all 51. |
| 52 total, 1 routed explicitly, default settings | Keeps the 1 routed connection and skips the remaining 51. |
| 52 total, 2 routed explicitly, default settings | Routes the remaining 50, completing all 52. |

This PR updates the documentation for existing core behavior. The regression also covers explicit overrides and nested subcircuits. [Core regression](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/blob/f7eccae522138ed2da3cbd97877aa0e411bd3f1e/tests/features/board-route-remaining-preflight.test.tsx) · [Preview the corrected board properties reference](https://docs-git-techmannih-document-remaining-routing-85e26d-tscircuit.vercel.app/elements/board#board-properties)

To reproduce in a core checkout, run `bun test tests/features/board-route-remaining-preflight.test.tsx`.

title: fix: ignore off-grid fiducials when estimating BGA pitch
description: Fixes incorrect BGA pitch estimation caused by off-grid fiducials, reducing unnecessary grid columns and improving mesh efficiency.
body:
Package fiducials make the STM32MP157 and A64 RAM grids infer **0.15 mm** spacing for **0.8 mm** BGA balls. This inserts unnecessary grid columns.

Choose an observed pitch that aligns more pad-coordinate pairs, preserving the existing estimate when it already fits. Pads, copper and routing rules are unchanged.

| STM32MP157 mesh | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inferred X pitch | 0.15 mm | 0.8 mm |
| Grid columns | 86 | 22 |
| Initial mesh nodes | 8,679 | 5,678 (−34.6%) |
| STM32 full merged regions | 115,983 | 91,890 (−20.8%) |
| Native mesh SVG | ![Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/1b563df80f427fbb85c588f24200fc41855550d8/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-stmp157-ram-bga-pitch.snap.svg) | ![After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/d794514/tests/repro/__snapshots__/pipeline9-stmp157-ram-bga-pitch.snap.svg) |

Stacked on repro #3718. This corrects the RAM mesh; STM32MP157 remains **32/72** connected and A64 **32/75**, with the remaining signals still failing path planning. The separate CPU duplicate-axis issue is unchanged.

<details><summary>DDR progress from the initial board runs</summary>

Initial means the first recorded run on November 6. Latest uses tscircuit 0.0.3168, Core 0.0.2354, autorouter 0.0.1085 and Bus 0.0.55.

| Board | Initial recorded result | Latest verified progress |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OrangeCrab | 50/50 connected | 50/50; zero clearance findings, 23 width warnings |
| H3 | 0/53 exported | 16/53; remaining path planning fails |
| A64 | 0/75 exported | 32/75 connected in an extended run; remaining 43 exhaust the planner budget |
| STM32MP157 | 0/72 exported | 32/72; remaining 40 exhaust the planner budget |
| A13 | 0/96 exported | 16/96 trace legs connected in an extended run, all on the CPU side; first RAM byte fails geometry and length matching |
| H616 | 0/53 exported | 53/53; 6 clearance findings, 23 width warnings |
| ButterStick | 0/55 exported | 55/55; zero clearance findings, 31 width warnings |
| Glider | 49/49 connected | 49/49; zero clearance findings, 14 width warnings |
| i.MX6 | 53/53 connected | 53/53; 5 clearance findings, no width warnings |
| iCEPi | 0/50 exported | 50/50; zero clearance findings, 27 width warnings |

120-second standard runs, plus extended qualification for completed boards, STM32, A64 and A13. Timings under concurrent investigation are not comparative benchmarks. These native DDR subsystems have not been qualified for timing or impedance.

</details>
