title: perf: reduce DDR mesh lookup work and retained state
description: Reduces the lookup work and retained state during DDR mesh construction, optimizing edge construction time and memory usage.
body:
Dense DDR meshes scan too many coarse-bucket candidates and retain construction caches throughout routing. Index node bounds with Flatbush, preserve the existing edge order, and release the lookup index and deduplication set after construction.

Stacked on #3687. The real A64 input, SVG and assertions are unchanged; the latest published Core emits the same byte-exact handoff.

| A64 captured mesh | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Edge construction | 8.262 s | 3.397 s (**2.43× faster**) |
| Retained JS heap after diagnostic GC | 172.07 MiB | 78.02 MiB (**−54.7%**) |
| Ordered edges | 347,143 | 347,143, byte-identical |

The heap row measures retained mesh-stage state, not peak process memory. Production does not force GC. This optimization preserves the graph; A64 still exhausts its later planner budget.

<details><summary>Benchmarks and native Core results</summary>

Same-machine Blacksmith comparisons, one sample worker and one routing thread, base `1a1deb2` versus head `b01d94e`:

| Dataset | Completed | DRC findings | P50 time | P95 time | Memory P80 |
| --- | --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| [SRJ18](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/43036682769) | 16/16 → 16/16 | 0 → 0 | **+0.8%** | −0.2% | **−9.6%** |
| [Dataset01](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/43036687900) | 85/85 → 85/85 | 0 → 0 | −2.7% | −0.1% | −0.5% |

Via counts are unchanged. SRJ18 timing is mixed: its median is slightly slower, while its memory use improves. Its summed measured stage time is 530.913 → 535.347 seconds (+0.8%); edge construction is 1.950 → 1.321 seconds. The benefit demonstrated here is dense DDR mesh construction and retained state.

The compiled fix was also installed into an isolated runtime using published `tscircuit@0.0.3157` / Core `0.0.2340`: the real H616 board still connects 53/53 signals with zero physical findings, and all 57 trace objects and 95 vias are byte-identical to published autorouter `0.0.1077`.

A separate A64/Core `0.0.2339` control measured edge construction at 11.420 → 4.439 seconds. Both runs retain identical 32 DQ traces and 44 vias before the remaining planner fails. Full-run peak RSS was 4560.5 → 4857.2 MiB in that single pair; the retained-heap reduction is not a demonstrated full-run peak-RSS reduction.

Build, full type checking, the unchanged native SVG/hash repro and focused edge tests pass locally. All PR CI checks are green. No formatter or linter was run locally.

</details>

<details><summary>Published DDR progress</summary>

Initial results are the first recorded ten-board Core run (November 6). Latest uses published `tscircuit@0.0.3157`, Core `0.0.2340`, bus solver `0.0.52` and autorouter `0.0.1077`; these release results are separate from this optimization.

| Board | Initial recorded result | Latest verified progress |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OrangeCrab | 50/50 signals connected | 50/50, zero physical findings |
| H3 | 0/53 exported | 16/53; remaining planner fails |
| A64 | 0/75 exported | 32 DQ complete; remaining 43 time out |
| STM32MP157 | 0/72 exported | 32 DQ complete; remaining 40 time out |
| A13 | 0/96 exported | First 8 DQ complete; next byte times out |
| H616 | 0/53 exported | 53/53, zero physical findings |
| ButterStick | 0/55 exported | 55/55 in extended run; physical findings 19 → 8 since 0.0.3154; 35 trace objects use source-plane layers |
| Glider | 49/49 connected | 49/49; 11 trace objects use a source-plane layer |
| i.MX6 | 53/53 connected | 53/53, zero physical findings |
| iCE/Pi | 0/50 exported | 50/50, zero physical findings |

Standard runs have a 120-second limit; ButterStick’s full run uses a 900-second budget and finishes in 534 seconds. Completed bus phases remain visible in stage artifacts when Core withholds final copper at timeout.

The experiment currently expresses source layer restrictions on buses; the remaining phase needs global/per-trace layer-policy support. That work is already covered by [Core #5370](https://github.com/tscircuit/core/pull/5370), so it is not duplicated here. ButterStick and Glider remain invalid under that source layer policy. DDR timing and electrical qualification are outside these checks.

</details>

title: Add a per-connection compute cost summary to the pipeline 9 solver
description: Adds getComputeCostSummary() to the pipeline 9 solver, providing a summary of compute costs for routing connections, aiding AI in identifying poorly placed components.
body:
Adds `getComputeCostSummary()` to the pipeline 9 solver (`AutoroutingPipelineSolver9_PreloadedTraceGraph`, and so also `_Networked`). It returns a frozen `ComputeCostSummary`: the hypergraph search iterations needed to route each connection pair alone, for the most expensive pairs. An AI placing parts can read it to find which parts are badly placed. ```ts type Iterations = number computeCostSummary: { metric: "hypergraph_route_search_iterations", measuredPairCount, // every pair measured, including ones cut from topPairs topPairs: [{ // highest first, at most 25 connectionName, rootConnectionNames, // every SRJ connection merged into this pair pcbPortIds, // measured endpoints; null for synthetic points iterations, // solo search iterations for this pair }], } ``` Route sections generated from copper laid by an earlier stage have no SRJ connection, so they are left out. This is the producer side of the core and cli events described in the architecture doc. Core reads it by duck typing, so no core change is needed in this repo. Seve's idea: tell the AI how much compute cost each connection takes, so it can spot bad placements. Stacked on tscircuit/tiny-hypergraph#315, which adds `DuplicateCongestedPortSolverReport.routeSearchIterations`. `package.json` pins tiny-hypergraph to `f953f0d` on `ohmx/route-search-iterations-autorouter-pin`: the #315 change applied on top of the currently pinned `a0a9a6c`. Repin after #315 merges. ### Where the number comes from The duplicate-congested-port pass, which already runs, routes every connection by itself before the real solve. A connection that has to detour around a rotated or swapped part needs many more search steps. ### Tests (TSX boards) - `tests/compute-cost/rotated-resistor-compute-cost.test.tsx`: R2 is rotated 180° beside a TSSOP-20. The top pair's endpoints include `R2.pin2` (71 iterations; the median is about 5). - `tests/compute-cost/multi-pin-net-compute-cost.test.tsx`: a four-pad GND net splits into more pairs than SRJ connections. Every pair keeps root names that exist in the SRJ, and its endpoints are real pcb ports. - `bunx tsc --noEmit` passes. ### Evidence - **Synthetic boards:** 66 boards, each with one part deliberately misplaced (swapped, rotated or moved resistors, or reversed headers). A part touching the most expensive connections was the misplaced part in 24/66 boards; random guessing gives ~8/66. Ranking by connection length gives 30/66, but this metric is strongest on rotated or swapped passives. Run through this API, the numbers match the prototype on all 66 boards. - **Real board** (`0hmX/dual-usb-peltier-assembly`, unrouted then autorouted): 3 rounds, each comparing a placement agent given this summary against one without it. The agents were Sol, Astra and Opus. The agent with the summary ended with fewer vias every round, all with 0 DRC errors: | Model | With summary | Without | |---|---|---| | Sol | 205 | 219 | | Astra | 211 | 214 | | Opus | 206 | 216 | The starting board had 231 vias. Three wins out of three would happen by chance 1 time in 8, and the noise is about ±7–10 vias, so this is suggestive, not proven. ### Not in this PR No routing behaviour changes. Nothing feeds the summary to an AI automatically yet: callers read it after `solve()`. Naming: this is called `computeCostSummary` rather than "effort", because `effort` already names the autorouter effort setting on these same events. Review changes (from Seve): `share` dropped, metric renamed to `hypergraph_route_search_iterations`, and the payload is `computeCostSummary` everywhere (events, cache entry, CLI output). There is no stage total: a sum over every connection grows with board size, so it is not a useful score. The snapshot is frozen all the way down. ### How compute cost reaches the CLI ```mermaid sequenceDiagram autonumber participant AR as autorouter pipeline 9 participant CM as core CapacityMeshAutorouter participant G as core Group stage participant CLI as cli AutorouterDiagnostics G->>CLI: autorouting:start G->>CM: start() Note over AR: solo pass runs while the port-point
stage is built, summary frozen once loop each progress tick, stepped or threaded CM->>AR: getComputeCostSummary() CM->>G: progress event with computeCostSummary G->>CLI: autorouting:progress (already spreads the event) end CM->>G: complete or error G->>CM: getComputeCostSummary() read directly, no tick needed G->>CLI: autorouting:end or autorouting:error with computeCostSummary CLI->>CLI: store under the stage key, include in debug output ``` 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

description: Removes redundant terminal paths between the same junctions on a power rail to eliminate unintended loops in schematics.

## Motivation

- Routing can leave two parallel wire paths between the same junctions on a power rail. The extra path adds no connection and makes the schematic look as though it contains an unintended loop. The larger loop reproduced in #1429 survives the existing cleanup because its path ends at a junction rather than a shared component pin.

- This adds a focused cleanup that removes a terminal segment only when other same-net paths already connect its ends and retain every attached pin, label, and branch. It uses connectivity rather than component names or coordinates.

##### Repro
-  #1429 


| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| A redundant terminal path remains alongside the power rail. | The extra terminal segment is removed while the existing connections remain. |
| The reproduction contains a large rail loop and a smaller internal junction loop. | The large rail loop is removed; the smaller junction loop is intentionally unchanged and remains covered by the reproduction. |

title: fix: align schematic connections to KiCad's grid
description: Built-in and custom symbols can place electrical endpoints between KiCads 1.27 mm connection-grid points. This addresses the off-grid portion of 878 by placing pins, symbol origins, and attached electrical objects together on every schematic sheet. Stacked on 893; this PR targets repro878-custom-symbol-off-grid. Solve sheet connections and local pin positions together, subject to attachment bounds on the unchanged symbol bodies. Choosing fixed local pin offsets first could reject valid layouts, including the automotive mirror fixture. Preserve coordinate ordering, but require a grid interval only where electrical points or wires must remain distinct. Unrelated wiring can share a row instead of forcing extra rows between another components pins. Check every electrical points wire attachments before applying placement. This permits diagonal wires whose contacts survive and rejects placements that would introduce or remove a connection. Determine pin attachments to circular arcs from their geometry, retaining the original arc span and branch. Symbols with unrelated arcs export normally. Recognize slanted free-end strokes as leads. Identical duplicate strokes move together; ambiguous attachments to different strokes still fail. Move wire endpoints, junctions, global and inline labels, and no-connect markers consistently. Prefer shared symbol definitions where the wiring permits them, and preserve already-aligned connections, including fractional-origin cases. Keep body artwork and scale unchanged; adjust lead endpoints or native pin lengths to reach the body. Use the existing coordinate helpers and transformation-matrix for placement. Surface unsatisfied placement constraints as errors. There is no warn-and-export-original-coordinates fallback. README documents the compatibility boundary: no body resizing or general rerouting, and KiCad only permits orthogonal native pin angles. Follow the maintainers cleanup requests: function-specific named parameters first and context last, hoisted helpers, domain-specific names and component-id types, numbered tests with tscircuit-built fixtures, and visual snapshots for all six built-in grid cases. No new dependencies. This does not implement general rerouting or resolve artworktext collisions; dense label text can still overlap. Validation with KiCad 10.0.1: Follow-up f3d658b: 21 focused grid and pin-angle tests pass locally. Three new regressions cover direct arc attachments, the missing part of an arc, and connected clockwise major arcs; native ERCnetlist checks and nine new PNG snapshots are included. Typecheck and formatting pass. Verified native KiCad rejects a generated file after changing a pin angle to 45 degrees. Normal converter paths already emit only cardinal pin angles. The existing graphics repro15 has the same local PNG mismatch with both the preceding and updated placement implementation; its expectation is unchanged. Full CI for the follow-up is pending. 34 tests pass, including the grid regressions, BGA pin-name compatibility, custom transistor, TB67S579FTG, inline labels, and all five generated systems. This was a normal run after updating and inspecting the affected snapshots. New numbered regressions cover independent pin rows sharing grid rows without merging four separate nets, duplicate slanted leads, and connected diagonal routing. Native KiCad netlist comparisons preserve all 584 net names and pin memberships across the BGA, automotive mirror, motor control, consumer wireless, Bluetooth audio, and blood-pressure monitor fixtures. Native ERC checks pass in the focused grid fixtures, excluding only embedded-library lookup warnings. The too-small-body test continues to require an explicit failure. Built-in and custom symbols can place electrical endpoints between KiCad's 1.27 mm connection-grid points. This addresses the off-grid portion of #878 by placing pins, symbol origins, and attached electrical objects together on every schematic sheet.

Stacked on #893; this PR targets `repro/878-custom-symbol-off-grid`.

- Solve sheet connections and local pin positions together, subject to attachment bounds on the unchanged symbol bodies. Choosing fixed local pin offsets first could reject valid layouts, including the automotive mirror fixture.
- Preserve coordinate ordering, but require a grid interval only where electrical points or wires must remain distinct. Unrelated wiring can share a row instead of forcing extra rows between another component's pins.
- Check every electrical point's wire attachments before applying placement. This permits diagonal wires whose contacts survive and rejects placements that would introduce or remove a connection.
- Determine pin attachments to circular arcs from their geometry, retaining the original arc span and branch. Symbols with unrelated arcs export normally.
- Recognize slanted free-end strokes as leads. Identical duplicate strokes move together; ambiguous attachments to different strokes still fail.
- Move wire endpoints, junctions, global and inline labels, and no-connect markers consistently. Prefer shared symbol definitions where the wiring permits them, and preserve already-aligned connections, including fractional-origin cases.
- Keep body artwork and scale unchanged; adjust lead endpoints or native pin lengths to reach the body. Use the existing coordinate helpers and `transformation-matrix` for placement.
- Surface unsatisfied placement constraints as errors. There is no warn-and-export-original-coordinates fallback. README documents the compatibility boundary: no body resizing or general rerouting, and KiCad only permits orthogonal native pin angles.
- Follow the maintainer's cleanup requests: function-specific named parameters first and context last, hoisted helpers, domain-specific names and component-id types, numbered tests with tscircuit-built fixtures, and visual snapshots for all six built-in grid cases.

No new dependencies. This does not implement general rerouting or resolve artwork/text collisions; dense label text can still overlap.

Validation with KiCad 10.0.1:

- Follow-up `f3d658b`: **21 focused grid and pin-angle tests pass locally**. Three new regressions cover direct arc attachments, the missing part of an arc, and connected clockwise major arcs; native ERC/netlist checks and nine new PNG snapshots are included. Typecheck and formatting pass.
- Verified native KiCad rejects a generated file after changing a pin angle to 45 degrees. Normal converter paths already emit only cardinal pin angles.
- The existing graphics repro15 has the same local PNG mismatch with both the preceding and updated placement implementation; its expectation is unchanged. Full CI for the follow-up is pending.

- **34 tests pass**, including the grid regressions, BGA pin-name compatibility, custom transistor, TB67S579FTG, inline labels, and all five generated systems. This was a normal run after updating and inspecting the affected snapshots.
- New numbered regressions cover independent pin rows sharing grid rows without merging four separate nets, duplicate slanted leads, and connected diagonal routing.
- Native KiCad netlist comparisons preserve all **584 net names and pin memberships** across the BGA, automotive mirror, motor control, consumer wireless, Bluetooth audio, and blood-pressure monitor fixtures.
- Native ERC checks pass in the focused grid fixtures, excluding only embedded-library lookup warnings. The too-small-body test continues to require an explicit failure.
- Exact SVG snapshots use the Linux KiCad drawing order from CI. Verified all 23 platform-dependent SVGs contain identical drawing primitives, coordinates, styles, and transforms to the macOS exports. Comparison assertions and tolerances are unchanged.
- [Full CI at `ff2a390`](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/actions/runs/42860572301): **306 tests pass, 0 fail**, across 266 files. Typecheck and formatting CI also pass.

Opened the exported fixtures from commit `b536bcc` in KiCad's schematic editor and inspected Net Navigator and ERC. These checks cover the two fixtures below; they are not a guarantee for every possible layout.

### Closely spaced custom-symbol pins

Net Navigator keeps A on `U1.1 / U2.1 / U3.1` and B on `U1.2 / U2.2`; `U3.2` remains intentionally unconnected. The branch junction and both separate nets survive grid placement. **Known visual limitation:** the A/B label text overlaps in this dense fixture; electrical connectivity is preserved, but label collision handling remains unfinished.

ERC reports zero errors and no off-grid or disconnected-pin warnings. The three remaining warnings concern the missing installed `Custom` library. Off-grid and disconnected-pin checks were enabled.

title: fix: tolerate floating-point roundoff in symbol artwork
description: Fixes floating-point roundoff issues in symbol artwork export, ensuring identical custom artwork exports as a single library definition.
body:
Identical custom artwork in #877 exports as two library definitions because placement and transformation put the same local coordinate on opposite sides of a KiCad rounding boundary. Treat artwork coordinates within the roundoff allowance of a half-unit boundary as ties; both instances now export as `Custom:MyPart`.

Use `transformSymbolPoint` in the five artwork converters. Hoist `roundSymbolCoordinate` and the roundoff factor to module scope, name the internal-unit scale, half-unit threshold and rounding-step count, and reuse `toSchematicInternalUnits` for ordinary rounding. Existing matrix types, `compose`, `applyToPoint`, `transformSchematicPoint`, pin placement and no-connect placement retain their behavior.

Circuit JSON provides custom artwork after placement, without the original local geometry. Subtracting the center before scaling still reproduces #877: the two instances yield local Y coordinates `0.07219` and `0.07218999999999998`, which round to `1.0829` and `1.0828` mm. Building directly from the original local geometry would require that geometry in the input; rearranging the existing transforms cannot recover it.

The allowance scales with the absolute matrix terms before cancellation, using `gamma_6 = 6u / (1 - 6u)`, where `u = Number.EPSILON / 2`. This uses the [accumulated-roundoff model](https://doi.org/10.1017/S0962492922000022), budgeting source conversion, placement, scaling the point and origin, subtraction, and conversion to KiCad units. It is a local allowance for this path, not a bound on arbitrary upstream geometry calculations. For the reported coordinate it is about `5.17e-14 mm`, versus KiCad's `0.0001 mm` grid. Nearby ties round away from zero; values outside the allowance use ordinary rounding. Stabilization is disabled if the allowance reaches half a native unit.

Keep one no-connect test per file: repro29 covers markers, repro30 covers connected pins, and repro31 covers parser rounding near a midpoint. Repro31 places the chip with `schY={0.00007}` through tscircuit, without editing Circuit JSON.

Stacked on #879. Merge the reproduction first, then retarget this PR to `main`.

The existing repro21 SVG updates cover three polarized-capacitor artwork coordinates rounding consistently from approximately ±0.75675 mm to ±0.7568 mm.

Validation:
- 9 focused regression tests pass, including native KiCad fractional-pin connectivity.
- Typecheck, build, formatting, and `git diff --check` pass.

- Full CI passes on `ef32b1f`: Bun Test, Type Check, and Format Check, including the automotive-mirror regression. [CI run](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-kicad/actions/runs/42848791997)

title: Avoid rail orientation advice for floating chip-return capacitors
description: Adds a guard to prevent incorrect rail orientation recommendations for floating chip-return capacitors in schematic analysis.
body:
## Problem

A chip pin marked `provides_power` can be a switching node. A capacitor between that output and another non-supply pin of the same chip can form a floating return, such as a bootstrap capacitor. The current rail and generic capacitor orientation rules still recommend a vertical supply-shunt layout even when there is no explicit power/ground net or voltage metadata.

## Change

Add a shared topology-and-metadata guard for this ambiguous local chip-return case and use it in both orientation solvers. The guard requires one power-providing port, a return to one non-supply pin on the same local chip, and no explicit rail, voltage, ground, or no-connect evidence. It does not inspect names, pin labels, or reference designators.

Keep orientation checks for explicit rails, ground/voltage declarations, additional supply sources or loads, multiple returns, different local scope, requires-power-only ports, and no-connect pins. This does not identify every bootstrap circuit or approve its placement.

## Reproduction and visuals

The same synthetic circuit is rendered before and after. Its circuit panel is pixel-identical; only the unsupported orientation recommendation disappears. Both images use the repository's stacked circuit/analysis convention.

**Before**
![Pristine analyzer recommends rotating the floating capacitor](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/c8e3d6b0c7794c39340c9958bfa334e9fef27512/tests/assets/floating-chip-capacitor/pristine-analysis.svg)

**After**
![Corrected analyzer leaves the circuit unchanged without the false warning](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-schematic-placement-analysis/c8e3d6b0c7794c39340c9958bfa334e9fef27512/tests/assets/floating-chip-capacitor/corrected-analysis.svg)

## Validation

- Pristine main `05b8dade`: the final floating regression fails with one generic orientation issue where zero is expected.
- Final focused tests: 2 passed, 999 assertions, four rotations, both capacitor pin orders, and 11 guard modes.
- Full canonical `bun test`: 341 passed, 0 failed, 19,759 assertions with the default timeout.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run build`: passed. Format reports four pre-existing oversized-fixture warnings.
- Final staged diff check passed. SVG trailing whitespace was normalized and focused visual tests remained green.
- Direct generic-solver guard assertions use a trace-free synthetic view while retaining source connectivity, to test this semantic rule independently of the existing inline-trace exemption. Normal pipeline snapshots retain the rendered traces.

One intermediate full run hit an existing drone test's 5-second timeout and an inline-dependent assertion in the new test. The assertion was corrected as described above; the final full run passed without changing timeouts or skipping tests.

Separate fix only. No board source, production dependencies, decoupling rules, or label-sizing behavior is changed.

title: Fix assembly preview cameras clipping tall and off-board models
description: Fixes camera clipping issues for tall and off-board models in assembly previews by adjusting camera positioning and margins without altering model geometry or introducing new dependencies.
body:
## Stack

**#27 (real reproduction) → this PR (camera fix).** Base: `repro/nema11-assembly-camera`. Merge the lower PR first, then retarget this one to main. Both are drafts.

## Correct native models, tighter framing

Both sides use the actual public NEMA11 controller/motor fixture and published **circuit-json-to-gltf 0.0.133**. That version already fixes the large motor's 16-bit index overflow, which caused the previously displayed distorted model. #27 updates the dependency, refreshed baselines and explicit 32-bit-index checks. This PR does not patch the exporter or alter model geometry.

| Output | Before (#27, same fixed exporter) | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Landscape 720×540 | ![NEMA11 landscape clipped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-3d-png/d553e92450c0d3c312b3e696d87738f120b399de/tests/__snapshots__/nema11-landscape.png) | ![Intact motor, tight landscape framing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-3d-png/a88c6742e4f1536a15192c0ff3782c61ebb3952e/tests/__snapshots__/nema11-landscape.png) |
| Portrait 540×720 | ![NEMA11 portrait clipped](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-3d-png/d553e92450c0d3c312b3e696d87738f120b399de/tests/__snapshots__/nema11-portrait.png) | ![Intact motor, tight portrait framing](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-3d-png/a88c6742e4f1536a15192c0ff3782c61ebb3952e/tests/__snapshots__/nema11-portrait.png) |

All **719,622 actual transformed vertices** are checked against PoppyGL's native view/projection:
- Landscape clipping: **7,012 → 0**
- Portrait clipping: **7,074 → 0**
- These refitted NEMA11 views fill **90% of the limiting image dimension**, with a 5% margin on each side. The prior world-box fit visibly filled only about 58% / 62%. This margin is not applied to already-fitting or custom cameras.
- The motor and its original leads stay in frame. The fixture's 10 mm exploded pose is for inspection, not manufacturing approval.

## Camera change

Fit the actual transformed mesh vertices instead of the empty corners of a world-axis bounding box. For a fixed direction/FOV, perspective-frustum constraints give a tight camera distance and target in one pass. This removes unnecessary white space without changing models, board dimensions, transforms or preset directions.

- Preserve the original camera when it already contains the scene, even when its existing margin is less than 5%. Only refitted views receive the minimum 5% margin.
- Explicit custom cameras remain untouched, including intentionally cropped views.
- Decode the exported GLB once and revoke its local object URL after loading.
- Preserve `getDefaultCameraForCircuitJson(circuitJson)` as the existing lightweight metadata-only helper, with no model loading. The explicit `getAssemblyCameraForCircuitJson(circuitJson, options?)` performs the costly full-model fit when a standalone camera is needed. README documents both.
- Ordinary-board, preset and custom-camera snapshots are **byte-identical to the upgraded repro branch**. The PCB color change belongs to the shared dependency update, not this camera fix.
- No new dependencies and no duplicate of glTF #291.

## Review follow-up: margins and performance

Both review concerns were confirmed and addressed in [a88c674](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-3d-png/commit/a88c6742e4f1536a15192c0ff3782c61ebb3952e).

- **Conditional margin:** README and JSDoc explicitly state that preserved views can have less than 5% margin. A regression test checks an already-fitting view with a 1% margin and verifies that the same camera is returned unchanged.
- **Compatibility and cost:** the original helper's metadata-only implementation is restored. A no-model-fetch regression fails against the previous entrypoint (one request) and passes with the fix (zero). The expensive path is a separately named, explicit API, not an automatic fallback.
- **PNG rendering:** unchanged. It still fits the scene it already loaded, so callers should render directly instead of calculating an assembly camera first and repeating conversion/loading. All native snapshots remain unchanged.

Measured warm medians on this workspace, five samples with fixture downloads excluded:

| Fixture | Metadata helper | Explicit assembly helper |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Small board | 0.004 ms | 155 ms |
| Real NEMA11 | 0.060 ms | 720 ms |

Exporting and decoding the GLB dominate this cost; NEMA11's vertex fit itself measured about 29 ms in a separate phase profile. These are illustrative local timings, not performance guarantees. Initial module loading, remote model downloads and other environments add variability. No fragile timing threshold or cache was added.

Reproduce with [`bun benchmarks/camera-helpers.ts`](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-3d-png/blob/a88c6742e4f1536a15192c0ff3782c61ebb3952e/benchmarks/camera-helpers.ts).

**Geometry proof:** both upgraded branches export the same **20,722,684-byte GLB**, SHA-256 `557aa958df3b376d48a7e8576cdbb523d58e4f5a2fc9c3f1f9c0a1d4e2cef6be`.

## Validation

- **51 tests pass**, including real NEMA11 native snapshots, valid large-mesh indices, zero-clipping and 90%-coverage assertions.
- All 10 presets plus default at landscape/portrait/square sizes; diagonal geometry regression; model-only and translated scenes; invalid/empty inputs; unchanged custom cameras.
- Full formatting, typecheck, dependency check, package build and browser bundle build pass locally.
- Exact head `a88c674`: **Bun Test, Type Check, Format Check and Dependency Check all passed in GitHub Actions**. No workflow changes were made for this review.
- Browser runtime remains unverified: the official Playwright Chromium download repeatedly returned a truncated/invalid archive. No browser-runtime pass is claimed.

Run `bun test tests/nema11-camera.visual.test.ts tests/assembly-camera.test.ts`. See the fixture README for checksums, source/licensing details and offline setup. No OEM source model bytes are committed.

Draft. Nothing merged.

title: feat: accept exact ordered lane hops in length matching
description: Ordered J1  ESD  MCU lanes now exclude TP1 and retain their declared hop order, allowing the matcher to add length to the shorter D J1  ESD hop instead of meandering both D hops.
body:
Ordered J1 → ESD → MCU lanes now exclude TP1 and retain their declared hop order. The matcher adds length to the shorter **D+ J1 → ESD hop**, rather than meandering both D− hops to match a root total that includes the tap.

| Measured copper (mm) | Captured input | Main/root output (#91) | Fixed/ordered output |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| D+ ordered hops | 20.414087 | 20.414087 | 21.645420 |
| D− ordered hops | 21.645420 | 25.996677 | 21.645420 |
| TP1 stub | 5.582590 | 5.582590 | 5.582590 |
| Actual lane skew | 1.231332 | 5.582590 | < 0.000001 |

Main selects `[0,1,3]` = `P_BC, tap, P_AB`. Ordered lanes select `[3,0]` = `P_AB, P_BC` and `[2,4]` = `N_AB, N_BC`. Fixed P_AB grows 11.768503 → 12.999835 mm (+1.231332); P_BC, both N hops and TP1 remain unchanged. Main had added +3.485240 mm to N_AB and +0.866018 mm to N_BC.

Before — actual main matcher output:

![Before: wrong D− meanders](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/87ffc50c97b953faf212b255eb0d87619af88ac9/tests/__snapshots__/ordered-usb-pair-length-matching.snap.svg)

After — ordered-lane output:

![After: D+ matched correctly](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/3e275d7781c8d169d9421c3e5286ac63f42e0674/tests/__snapshots__/ordered-usb-pair-length-matching.snap.svg)

**The same passing test file and same `tests/__snapshots__/ordered-usb-pair-length-matching.snap.svg` path are updated**, so GitHub shows a before/after image diff. The input-only and extra fix-only pictures are removed. The exact-hop `test.failing` is now a normal test; missing/ambiguous-hop coverage remains. Snapshots are outside expected-failure tests on both branches.

The fixture is captured from [real TSX source](https://github.com/tscircuit/length-matching-solver/blob/3e275d7781c8d169d9421c3e5286ac63f42e0674/tests/fixtures/ordered-usb-pair.board.tsx). Pictures use only `convertCircuitJsonToPcbSvg` and `toMatchSvgSnapshot` with native silkscreen and fabrication-note captions above the copper. The captions describe ordered hops and format result lengths directly from the test measurements; only the rendered board outline is extended to fit them. Both PNGs were inspected: the incorrect large lower-left D− meander and right D− bump disappear; two smaller D+ bends appear between J1 and ESD.

Implementation accepts nonempty ordered exact-hop lists alongside legacy root strings. Resolved indexes remain attached through existing meander planning; no meander algorithm, coupling, ownership or SRJ field changes. Stack: main → #91 → this fix; required by tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter#3710.

Validation on Bun 1.4.3: snapshot update and rerun without updates pass. All 3 touched USB tests plus small-gap and linear-regression tests pass: **5 tests / 37 assertions**. Repository TypeScript and Biome format pass. Structural checks have 0 errors, with existing short-file/folder-size advisories. No full-suite/performance claim for this update. Draft; never merged.

title: Skip distant pads before DDR meander clearance checks
description: Reduces DDR length matching time by skipping distant pads and their connectivity checks, resulting in an 8.4 speedup in tuning time without altering emitted copper or routing rules.

title: fix: respect blind via layers when routing local HDMI escapes
description: Fixes routing failures for local HDMI escapes by ensuring proper handling of blind and buried vias, allowing for four pad-to-via escapes without clearance violations.
body:
The captured MT8395 HDMI request rejected every local escape because bottom decoupling pads were checked against top-to-inner4 blind vias. It now produces all **four pad-to-via escapes**, with zero clearance violations against the full board and all 138 fixed DDR routes.

Candidate vias, source stubs, supplied traces/vias, and cross-component assignments are checked only where their physical copper layers intersect. Local escapes read `inputSrj.allowBlindAndBuriedVias ?? false` directly; the duplicate routing option has been removed. Omitted or `false` produces physical through vias spanning every board layer, including clearance checks against bottom pads. Only explicit `true` permits blind/buried spans. Supplied via metadata cannot enable that capability: a narrower physical span with the flag off is rejected as inconsistent input, without rewriting fixed copper. Regression coverage includes all three SRJ settings and conflicting supplied-via metadata.

Stacked on #271: the same three snapshots show the old behavior in that PR and the improvement here. The main snapshot draws actual emitted copper and includes the relevant board TSX.

![After: four HDMI local escapes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/1c726cc7cfdd2ce0c93b928a133b918d301dcdf4/tests/__snapshots__/mt8395-hdmi-blind-vias.snap.svg)

Validation:
- Exact core request: four escapes, zero full-board clearance issues, all four pad-to-handoff paths connected; input hash unchanged.
- Small controls: off-span pads/traces/vias no longer block; in-span copper and through vias still block; opposite-side disjoint spans can share XY.
- Existing local-dogbone, matching, and via-connectivity tests pass.
- Full typecheck passes (`NODE_OPTIONS=--max-old-space-size=8192 bun run typecheck`). The final-revision paired local benchmark is complete; see the full comparison below.

This fixes the local escape stage. The full HDMI bus-lanes request now gets past that stage but still reaches a later dense-grid search budget limit; this PR does not claim a fully routed HDMI interconnect.

The final CI benchmark rerun is green and its artifacts are available: [base run](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/actions/runs/43092598555) / [head run, attempt 2](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/actions/runs/43093881945/attempts/2). Both completed all 72 cases at concurrency 32 and a 120-second per-case budget: **29 solved, 43 timeouts**, with identical per-case status and solved-case routed/validated counts, via counts, and attempts. Wall time: 246.692 s base, 252.618 s head. No speedup claim. The earlier failed artifact upload was recovered by rerunning the same pinned revision.

Paired local benchmark: base `51f050e8166e89fa7d27b32d5fd81c552a425f0e`, head `1c726cc7cfdd2ce0c93b928a133b918d301dcdf4`. All 72 captured inputs are byte-identical. Wall time was 1532.488 s base and 1530.046 s head; no speedup is claimed from this single run.

Reproduction: run `./benchmark.sh --concurrency 4 --sample-timeout-seconds 120 --output-directory <output>` in each pinned checkout, sequentially on the same Linux x64 host with Bun 1.4.4. title: test: reproduce HDMI blind escapes blocked by bottom copper
description: Reproduces the issue where HDMI blind escapes are blocked by bottom decoupling pads, providing comprehensive tests and validation without altering the solvers production.
body:
The MT8395 HDMI request cannot create any local pad escapes because bottom decoupling pads are treated as blockers for top-to-inner4 blind vias.

This reproduction retains the complete core input: both HDMI signals, every obstacle, and all 138 supplied DDR traces. The fixture is losslessly compressed and its restored SHA-256 is checked. Three passing tests capture the existing failure, with matching before snapshots for the real board, layer-obstacle controls, and opposite-side via spans. The board image includes the relevant TSX and highlights the unconnected CPU pads.

![Before: missing HDMI escapes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/51f050e8166e89fa7d27b32d5fd81c552a425f0e/tests/__snapshots__/mt8395-hdmi-blind-vias.snap.svg)

Validation: all eight test shards and the aggregate test check pass on final head `3f7ceba7`; typecheck, formatting, and runner smoke checks also pass. [Final CI run](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/actions/runs/43130910878). All three reproduction tests pass against the unchanged solver. No solver production changes. The shard runner now gives each test file a fresh Bun process to avoid retaining large fixtures across files; assertions, snapshots, and shard assignment are unchanged. The K230 top-right-offset regression has a 600-second test limit after an isolated CI run took 367 seconds and exceeded its prior 240-second cap; the separate 120-second routing benchmark limit is unchanged. The runner's selection, continued execution after failure, and exit status were smoke-tested. These tests cover local pad-to-via escapes; they do not assert a completed HDMI interconnect.

Stack dependency: based on #262 (`fix/owned-via-layer-connectivity`), which supplies the physical-via-span connectivity helper. The separate fix is #272; it replaces these same three snapshots with validated local escapes.

title: Respect physical via layers in endpoint connectivity
description: Fixes endpoint connectivity to respect a vias physical layers, allowing connections through the barrel beyond logical layer transitions.
body:
Endpoint connectivity ignored a via’s physical `layers`, rejecting branches that connect through the barrel beyond its logical `from_layer`/`to_layer` transition. Reuse and export the existing physical-span helper, preserving endpoint-derived spans when metadata is absent.

One inline test covers through barrels, partial spans, legacy metadata, and input immutability. Validation: the full eight-shard CI test suite and aggregate check pass on the updated branch, along with format and type checks. The 25 focused tests also passed.

Stacked on #252 to match bus-lanes-solver’s current pinned source.

title: Add local signal dogbones for fixed-layer bus routing
description: Adds routeLocalSignalDogbones for routing both package terminals to local signal-layer vias before a fixed-layer interconnect solve, preserving existing boundary-routing behavior.
body:
Adds `routeLocalSignalDogbones` for routing both package terminals to local signal-layer vias before a fixed-layer interconnect solve. Endpoints already reachable on the target layer do not get another via. The existing `FanoutSolver` boundary-routing contract is unchanged.

The primitive reuses component dogbone site matching, preserves circular pads, accounts for fixed copper and full through-via spans, tolerates imported grid rounding when constructing candidate sites, and checks cross-component escape collisions. It throws atomically on an impossible assignment and leaves the input unchanged.

Validation:
- Focused SVG test: 94 assertions pass, including both package ends, all four cardinal rotations, top/bottom source layers, immutable input, already-reachable terminals, and a blocking pad on another through-via layer.
- Typecheck passes. The new SVG and core integration snapshot were visually inspected.
- Updated against current main. All eight CI test shards and the aggregate check pass, along with format and type checks. Focused local-dogbone, imported-grid, and layer regressions pass (7 tests, 2,297 assertions).

This supplies the local fanout primitive for the bus_lanes integration. The full AM3352 bus-routing regression remains under development in the dependent solver/core work.

title: fix: generate exact-angle dogbone sites for imported pad grids
description: Fixes failure to assign valid dogbone sites for pads in imported STM32MP157DAB1 footprint, ensuring all pads have legal candidates for routing.
body:
Found while building our four-motor USB-PD motherboard with an imported STM32MP157DAB1 footprint (JLCPCB C1236721). The midpoint-only candidate generator can reject a rounded grid's diagonal as non-45-degree without considering nearby legal 45-degree positions. In #267, ten of the 354 pads have no candidate and the complete assignment fails.

This adds intersections of each source pad's 45-degree rays with adjacent interstitial rows/columns for plane-terminated dogbones. Every new position passes the existing pad, trace, via, fixed-copper and mutual-clearance checks. Pad coordinates and geometry tolerances are unchanged. Matching tries the existing midpoint sites first, then expands only if that component has no complete assignment; both passes share the existing search-state limit.

**Stack:** #267 → this PR. The base is `repro/imported-grid-via-sites`. This fanout change can merge independently of [dogbone-solver #17](https://github.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/pull/17). It uses the existing plane-termination API and does not depend on the proposed local-signal API in #252.

The full-footprint test now expects all **354/354** assignments and independently audits their straight stubs and through-vias against all captured obstacles. The snapshot shows the entire pad field and an enlarged A10. These are synthetic per-pad geometry requests, not the motherboard netlist.

| Before (#267) | After |
| --- | --- |

title: feat: fit demand-sized tuning banks to a populated board
description: Fits demand-sized tuning banks to a populated board by allowing kinks in routing paths and adjusting bank layouts to accommodate obstacles from other components.
body:
Stacked on #177 (base branch `feat/demand-sized-tuning-banks`).

## Fit the tuning banks to a populated board

On the full AM3352 + DDR3 SBC, keeping the matched DDR buses off the ground and power plane layers failed below 27 mm on every revision. Replaying the length-matching stage of 24 captured failing states showed two causes that have nothing to do with how much room the banks need.

**A kink read as a hairpin.** Several lanes step 0.05 mm sideways past a RAM fanout via and continue in the same direction. `tuningPathIsSelfClear` judged the two straight pieces around that step as returning arms closer than the spacing. That one lane then rejected every bank layout on its layer, every meander on itself and, if matching still got through, the finished route (`Final self-clearance violation`). 16 of the 24 captured states contained such a lane.

**Other parts' copper inside the tuning window.** The window starts just outside the SoC's own pad field. On the full board, decoupling-capacitor vias and a resistor's via and pads sit in the first 2 mm of it, and the banks ran into them.

**Change.**

- `tuningPathIsSelfClear` takes `allowKinks`. Two segments that bypass less copper than the spacing itself (and at least a tenth of it) and do not head back toward each other are one copper body, not a returning arm. A hairpin with a short turn reverses direction and stays rejected, crossings are never exempted, and sub-micron backsteps stay rejected so `tests/normalize-bottom-carrier-tail.test.ts` holds unchanged. `tests/tuning-path-kinks.test.ts` covers the routed kink, a hairpin, a crossing and such a backstep.
- The final validation in `BusLanesSolver` allows kinks. Nothing else changes for existing candidates: bank spreading and both tuners stay strict unless asked.
- `spreadCoupledTuningLanes` takes `boardAware`. When no bank layout fits the whole window it moves the window's ends past the supplied copper that blocked a bank and tries again, and it accepts kinks in the routed approaches. The body of its trim loop moved into a closure for this; without the flag the same windows are tried in the same order.
- `match()` yields one more candidate after all existing ones: demand-sized banks with `boardAware` on, tuned with kinks allowed.

Two further ideas were tried and removed because no captured state needed them: banks placed in lane order across the corridor instead of nested outward, and judging only added copper. They are not in this PR.

## On the full board

Same board and capture method as #173 and #177 ([repros/am3352-ddr3-sbc](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/tree/24a9e6de2a321cf5ee2b54713342085f951d3214/repros/am3352-ddr3-sbc)): 50 signals, 782 pad and hole obstacles, 259 fixed fanout vias, one view per copper layer. "Before" is the base branch (#177).

**RAM 25 mm below the SoC, the three matched buses kept off both plane layers**

| Base (#177): fails, 0/50 | This branch: 50/50, DRC and matching passed |
| --- | --- |
| ![Failed baseline](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/6c0dfde2a8a90560d8bf9f8497195574f6367427/repros/am3352-ddr3-sbc/ddr-25mm-off-planes.png) | ![Completed](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/24a9e6de2a321cf5ee2b54713342085f951d3214/repros/am3352-ddr3-sbc/ddr-25mm-off-planes.png) |

**Already routed on the base, now on an earlier layer attempt with different copper**

| | Base (#177) | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 27 mm, off the plane layers | ![Base](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/01d16c36b5d7a330430f1da7457d2263d9813b15/repros/am3352-ddr3-sbc/ddr-27mm-off-planes.png) | ![This branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/24a9e6de2a321cf5ee2b54713342085f951d3214/repros/am3352-ddr3-sbc/ddr-27mm-off-planes.png) |
| 19 mm, all six layers | ![Base](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/01d16c36b5d7a330430f1da7457d2263d9813b15/repros/am3352-ddr3-sbc/ddr-19mm.png) | ![This branch](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/24a9e6de2a321cf5ee2b54713342085f951d3214/repros/am3352-ddr3-sbc/ddr-19mm.png) |

`tests/am3352-ddr3-sbc-25mm-off-planes.test.ts` is new. It asserts completion and every acceptance check but does not compare its picture: GitHub's runners route this capture (50/50, with the same copper length per layer as the recorded route) yet did not reproduce the recorded picture pixel for pixel. The same Bun build in Debian 13 and Ubuntu 26.04 x64 containers reproduces it exactly, so the difference comes from the runner hardware. The picture in the repository is the container's, written only after all checks passed. The 27 mm and 19 mm snapshots are updated and are compared on CI; the 20 mm snapshot is unchanged ([snapshot diffs](https://github.com/tscircuit/bus-lanes-solver/commit/24a9e6de2a321cf5ee2b54713342085f951d3214)). The 25 mm baseline was recorded with the base branch's solver on Linux x64 (commit `6c0dfde`).

Full-board results by chip spacing. Linux x64 with all acceptance checks where marked, otherwise solved standalone on macOS arm64:

| Full board | Base (#177) | This branch |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Off the plane layers, 20, 21, 22, 23 mm | fails | fails |
| Off the plane layers, 24 mm | fails (Linux) | routes (Linux, checks passed, not a test) |
| Off the plane layers, 25 mm | fails (Linux) | routes (Linux, test) |
| Off the plane layers, 27 mm | routes (Linux, test) | routes (Linux, test) |
| Off the plane layers, 30 mm | routes | routes |
| All six layers, 17 and 18 mm | fails | fails |
| All six layers, 19 and 20 mm | routes (Linux, tests) | routes (Linux, tests) |
| All six layers, 21, 22, 23, 24, 25, 27 mm | routes | routes |

**Not addressed.** Off the plane layers still fails at 20 to 23 mm. In those states the DQS and CK pairs find no room for their meander (`No shared tuning corridor`, `Coupled tuning candidate budget exhausted`); in the 21 mm state inspected the tuning window between the SoC pad field and the RAM escape vias was 7 mm long. At 24 mm the first layer attempt matches and then fails when the package-coupling step needs to re-tune one DQS rail; the second attempt completes, which is why that solve takes 10 to 14 minutes.

Test time on Linux x64: the new 25 mm test takes about 4 minutes; the 27 mm test drops from about 12 to about 6 minutes and the 19 mm test from about 3 to about 1.5.

## Validation

- On Linux x64 (Bun 1.4.4, the CI runtime, in a container) at the head commit with the committed snapshots: the four full-board tests (`20mm`, `19mm`, `25mm-off-planes`, `27mm-off-planes`), `tests/am3352-ddr3-signal-layers-only.test.ts`, `tests/am3352-ddr3-pair-gap-at-clearance.test.ts` and `tests/tuning-path-kinks.test.ts` pass. The 19 mm and 25 mm snapshots were recorded and then matched again in a separate run.
- 24 mm off the plane layers on Linux x64: solved, then checked outside the test suite for connectivity (309/309 including the fanouts) and copper DRC (0 issues); bus skew 0.635 mm on all three buses, pair skew within 0.127 mm.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run format:check` pass.
- Full suite on macOS arm64 at `24a9e6d`: 596 pass, 0 fail across 229 files. The head commit `66ecb24` changes two test files only.
- CI at `66ecb24`: all checks pass, including both `test` jobs and `AM3352 benchmark (11/11)`. The first push (`24a9e6d`) failed both `test` jobs at the 25 mm picture comparison described above; nothing else failed.
- Not verified: an end-to-end `tsci build` with this solver. All results are from the solver run on dumped Core phase inputs.

## Benchmark effect

Base `01d16c3` (head of #177) against this branch, in two runs:

1. A paired run, both revisions concurrently, of the base and of this branch one step before its final form (working tree `3d49ab3`).
2. A run of the final code on its own afterwards (tree `f8b8feb`; the head commit `24a9e6d` has the same `lib/` and tests and differs only in the README). It differs from `3d49ab3` only in that the kink exemption no longer covers sub-micron backsteps. Its result file is identical to the paired head run in every non-timing field, including all iteration counts.

All three result sets solved **11/11** samples, each with **47/47 signals** (517/517 in total), **0 fixed or combined copper DRC findings** and all validation checks passing. Every trace length, skew, pair gap and quality metric is identical between base and head on all eleven samples.

**One sample is slower.** `inner-layers-right` reaches the same final route with 384,114 iterations instead of 159,783, and in the paired run took 132 s instead of 83 s. In an intermediate matching stage where every existing candidate fails, the new candidate now matches and passes the kink-tolerant final check; the work that follows is later discarded in favour of the same route as before. Disabling either the new candidate or the kink-tolerant final check brings that sample back to 159,783 iterations. The other ten samples have identical iteration counts.

Paired run:

| Metric | Base `01d16c3` | Head (`3d49ab3` tree) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Samples solved and validated | 11/11 | 11/11 |
| Median solve time | 82.749 s | 132.331 s |
| Sum of sample solve times | 2369.988 s | 2413.095 s |

| Sample | Base s | Head s | Iterations (base / head) | Bus skew, mm | Pair skew, mm |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | --- |
| control | 33.581 | 34.068 | 50026 | 0.635000 / 0.635000 | 0.077868 / 0.126884 / 0.072830 |

title: fix: use blind-via-aware escapes for native HDMI routing
description: Fixes HDMI routing failure due to local blind-via escapes being rejected by bottom-layer decoupling pads, updating the fanout-solver to check physical via spans and source-trace layers.
body:
The MT8395 HDMI request fails before routing because local blind-via escapes are rejected by bottom-layer decoupling pads. Update the pinned fanout-solver revision from `e202cef` to `1c726cc`, which checks physical via spans and source-trace layers. Local escapes now read `inputSrj.allowBlindAndBuriedVias ?? false` directly; callers no longer pass a separate option or derive permission from existing vias. Supplied blind-via metadata is rejected when the SRJ flag is off. Depends on https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/pull/272, stacked on the exact-input reproduction https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/pull/271. Those PRs include the complete captured core input and corresponding before/after snapshots with relevant TSX. Four local pad escapes replace the previous assignment failure, with no clearance issues against the supplied DDR copper. Validation: the installed pinned dependency builds successfully; isolated Node, browser, and TypeScript package consumers pass. The full CI suite passes: 590 tests, zero failures, 572,000 assertions. All 11 targeted routing tests and typecheck also pass. The existing fallback tests now explicitly block all candidate via sites; bottom pads under a top-only stub are no longer treated as a via obstruction. A new assertion validates all 94 local escapes on the unchanged AM3352 board against its fixed copper with zero clearance issues. The AM3352 provenance test replays its original generator through a pinned development dependency, preserving the saved power copper and its provenance. The H3 snapshot is refreshed after validating all 11 connections and zero DRC, drill-overlap, or route-quality issues. Benchmark effect: **11/11 freshly solved and accepted on both base and head**, with complete connectivity, zero DRC issues, passing bus/pair skew and coupling, and preserved fixed copper. Validation metrics are identical for every sample. No lost completions or quality regressions were observed. Individual solve times increased for `left`, `inner-layers-left`, and `control-inner1`; other cases decreased. These are single paired measurements, so no general speedup is claimed. The Blacksmith workflow uses Bun 1.4.0 on Linux x64 with 4 vCPUs per sample, the pinned base harness and identical inputs, and a 3600-second per-solver/sample limit. Reproduce with `bun base/scripts/pr-benchmark/run-pair.ts --sample --timeout-seconds 3600 --main base/lib/index.ts --pr head/lib/index.ts --main-sha ca541dac09c149ca73ddaa456fc263fcdb183073 --pr-sha 447aefec590ddd7c4ed9e3a463f4123e6d4641db --controller-sha ca541dac09c149ca73ddaa456fc263fcdb183073 --output results/.json`. The first attempt's two failed artifact uploads were recovered by fresh paired reruns, without changing code or budgets.

title: Choose reachable trunk vias for RAM branches
description: Compares reachable via anchors with the existing multi-goal grid search before routing the branch to optimize the selection of trunk vias for RAM branches.
body:
ButterStick chose the nearest trunk via by straight-line distance. Its second-RAM detour crossed the FPGA pad field and blocked UDM. Compare reachable via anchors with the existing multi-goal grid search before routing the branch. Stacked on #178; the fixture, test assertions, pad geometry and fabrication rules are unchanged. This overlaps #8/#9: the same candidate/emitter contract mismatch, with coverage for a real imported STM32 grid. Fix #17 is stacked **on top of this repro**, with the accepted-route snapshot. Merge/review order: #16 → #17.

title: test: reproduce reserved-plane dogbone escape failure
description: Reproduces a failure in the dogbone escape routing when a ground plane is reserved, confirming the defect with a comprehensive test.
body:
With fanout `0.0.79`, a top-layer SIGNAL escape succeeds with an ordinary inner1 GND pour but fails when the same pour is reserved with `unbroken={true}`. This PR records that defect using native solver output. The issue was found while building our STM32MP157D 4-Motor USB-C / USB-PD Control Motherboard.

**Stack: `main → this repro PR (#10) → dependency/fix PR #11`.** This PR targets `main` and keeps fanout at `0.0.79`. #11 is based on this branch and updates fanout to `0.0.82`, together with the success assertions and fixed snapshot. Merge this repro first, then retarget #11 to `main`.

![Original failure with the reserved ground plane](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/cb2891ef11e0fe62c3f19912b53cd7fe7e228fbe/tests/__snapshots__/unbroken-plane.snap.svg)

One test runs the two unchanged constructor inputs captured from stock core 0.0.2323 / props 0.0.724. It verifies that the reserved pour is the only input difference, the control produces one escape trace and via, and the reserved case reports `No complete local dogbone assignment within clearance/search limits`. Passing this test confirms the original defect is reproduced.

The standalone TSX example explicitly lists all nine pads. `routeRemaining={false}` isolates local escape. The snapshot uses `solver.visualize()` with captions and enlarged views; no saved routes, solver-input patches, or invented output copper are used. The examples are excluded from this solver-only tsconfig because it has no core JSX runtime/types; the TSX was separately rendered and typechecked when the inputs were captured. No dependencies are added or updated.

The obsolete `tests/unbroken-plane.md` is removed. To recapture, copy the two files in `examples/` into a tscircuit project and run `bun examples/capture-unbroken-plane.mjs`; the script observes native solver events.

Validation with published fanout `0.0.79`, without `bun link`:
- `bun test`: 14 passing tests, 0 failures, 1,032 assertions.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `git diff --check`: pass.

Upstream fix: [tscircuit/fanout-solver#264](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/pull/264). This local escape repro does not establish full-board routing or rendered antipad correctness.

title: fix: constrain dogbone candidates before assigning imported grid escapes
description: Fixes angle-selection mismatch for dogbone candidates in STM32MP157DAB1 native escape, ensuring only valid 45-degree candidates are assigned.
body:
Stacked **on top of #16**. Merge/review order: repro #16 → this fix.

The STM32MP157DAB1 native escape from our four-motor USB-PD motherboard selected a non-45-degree candidate, then failed its own angle guard. Ask the existing fanout matcher for its plane/direct candidate geometry so unsupported angles are removed before joint assignment. This matches dogbone's local pad-to-via operation. The signal's net and target layer are unchanged; this does not connect it to a power plane.

This is the same production change already proposed in #9 by @seveibar. The separate stack adds the full imported STM32 footprint reproduction requested in #16 and its before/after snapshot. No footprint coordinates, tolerances, clearance rules or saved routes are changed; the emission guard remains in place.

For W13, the selected via changes from (6.799961, 1.999996) to (6.799961, 2.799969) mm. Both X/Y offsets are now 0.399923 mm. The unchanged captured input produces one 0.15 mm trace and one 0.30/0.15 mm through-via, logically handing off from top to inner3.

Validation: all 15 tests pass (1053 assertions), typecheck and formatting pass. The updated regression checks endpoint/net identity, via dimensions and all six spanned layers, input immutability, and an independent emitted-copper audit against all original physical pads. The reserved ground plane remains in the solver input; downstream pour-antipad generation is outside that physical-pad audit. Updated SVG rendered and inspected. Only the solver line/comment, this regression test and its snapshot change relative to #16.

Follow-up investigation of the native 260-connection MCU capture confirms an additional candidate-generation limitation in [fanout-solver](https://github.com/tscircuit/fanout-solver/blob/a17d71b93e3794d76e1b13a3ecf5c91ba616c6aa/lib/match-component-dogbone-via-sites.ts#L361). Its midpoint-only enumeration plus exact-angle filter leaves four connections with zero candidates; distinct-site matching can cover at most 171/260 requests even before inter-route clearance. Increasing the search budget to one million states does not help.

For diagnosis only, nearby exact-45° sites (maximum movement 0.000127 mm) were supplied through the matcher's public fixed-site API. All original pads and clearance rules were retained. A complete 260-site assignment was accepted and its constructed geometry passed the physical-pad/copper audit (260 traces, 260 vias, no issues; pour antipads remain outside this audit). The analogous 354-pad geometry diagnostic also passed with supplied sites. These are feasibility witnesses, **not automatically generated dogbone output or saved board routes**. Native MCU routing remains blocked until candidate generation is addressed. This PR continues to cover only the angle-selection mismatch.

![Accepted native W13 escape](https://github.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/blob/fix/imported-grid-angle/tests/__snapshots__/imported-grid.snap.svg?raw=true)

title: fix: configure GitHub Packages after dependency installation
description: Fixes the GitHub Packages configuration in the release workflow to ensure dependencies are installed correctly before publishing.
body:
The release workflow configures the entire `@tscircuit` scope to use GitHub Packages before `bun install`. In [the failed release job](https://github.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/actions/runs/42970561135/job/130357801999), installation then requests dependencies from `npm.pkg.github.com` and receives 401/404 responses, so build and publish never run.

Keep Node 20 setup before installing tools and dependencies, and configure the GitHub Packages registry in a separate setup-node step after `bun run build`, immediately before publishing. Installs use the normal npm registry; the publish step retains its existing registry scope and authentication.

Only `.github/workflows/bun-pver-release-ghp.yml` changes.

Validation:
- Workflow YAML parses; verified that dependency installation and build precede registry configuration and publishing.
- Fresh checkout: `bun install --no-cache` succeeds, installing all 338 packages.
- [Bun Test CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/actions/runs/42971516299): passes after a successful clean install; 14 tests, 0 failures, 1,034 assertions.
- [Type Check CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/actions/runs/42971516325) and [Format Check CI](https://github.com/tscircuit/dogbone-solver/actions/runs/42971516301): pass.
- Local `bun run build` and `git diff --check`: pass.

The first CI attempts encountered a separate 404 for the public npm `lucide-react@1.72.0` tarball. Once the same tarball became available, the uncached installation and all three CI retries passed on this unchanged commit. No dependency pins, overrides, or bypasses were added.

Live publishing was not triggered; the release job runs after this workflow change lands on `main`.

title: Estimate JLCPCB small-via drilling surcharges
description: Add the small-via drilling surcharge to rigid FR-4 quotes, check drill and pad sizes to ensure compliance, update testing estimates, and accept empty pick-and-place files for bare-board quotes.
body:
## Summary

- Add the small-via drilling surcharge to rigid FR-4 quotes. Use the smallest qualifying drill and apply its rate once per order.
- Check every drill and pad size in the fabrication files so a smaller exempt via cannot hide a chargeable one. Apply JLCPCB's wide-pad exemption where it qualifies.
- Update the separate 4-wire Kelvin testing estimate using the calculator and account for the higher Y45 review supplement in the estimate range.
- Accept empty pick-and-place files on bare-board quotes, which the Circuit JSON exporter generates for boards without components.

## Pricing evidence

JLCPCB's calculator showed these USD line items for 70 × 70 mm FR-4 boards on November 12, 2026. The rates fit a base fee plus the total ordered board area using the two order sizes. [JLCPCB calculator](https://cart.jlcpcb.com/quote) · [FR-4 via capabilities](https://jlcpcb.com/capabilities/pcb-capabilities)

| Line item | 5 boards | 100 boards |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| 0.25 mm drill surcharge | $16.95 | $24.65 |
| 0.20 mm drill surcharge | $17.15 | $28.70 |
| 0.15 mm drill surcharge | $34.30 | $57.40 |
| 4-wire Kelvin testing | $16.87 | $23.03 |

The upper Kelvin estimate uses the $54.18 supplement requested for Y45 when it exceeds the calculator estimate. [Order observations](https://github.com/tscircuit/jlcpcb-manufacturing-specs/blob/main/datasets/jlcpcb/supplement-observations.json)

## Verification

- `bun test` passed all 40 tests, including the pricing tiers, the 0.30 mm boundary, and a bare-board Circuit JSON quote with mixed via sizes.
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check`, and `bun run build:site` passed.

title: Show a summary table of every expense, check assembled quantities
description: Adds a summary table displaying all expenses, including total and per-board prices, and enforces that assembled boards do not exceed PCB quantity.

title: Faster part lookups, lead-free default, fixed sales tax, no false paste warning
description: Implements faster part lookups by fetching BOM lines in batches, sets lead-free HASL as the default surface finish, removes false warnings for bottom paste openings on through-hole pins, and displays the sales tax rate on the quote page without allowing edits.
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #2, which was merged just before this commit was pushed.

- **Faster part lookups.** BOM lines are looked up eight at a time, and each part's jlcsearch record and footprint are fetched together. jlcsearch overload answers (HTTP 500, "too many resources consumed within a 10 second window") are retried in short, growing steps of 0.5s instead of 2s. A 73-part board now takes 2 to 17 seconds instead of about 60; the spread comes from jlcsearch's database occasionally reporting overload.
- **Lead-free HASL by default**, in the library and on the quote page. There is no lead-free price for 6- and 8-layer boards yet, so those now need an explicit finish.
- **No warning for bottom paste on through-hole pins.** tscircuit exports paste openings on the bottom end of the pins of top-side through-hole parts, which produced a "paste openings on the bottom but no parts placed there" warning on single-sided boards. body:
## Summary

Replaces the placeholder with a working JLCPCB quote estimator. Given Circuit JSON it returns an itemised estimate of bare PCBs, the charges JLCPCB engineers add after review, assembly fees and parts, each with a low/high range and a confidence label. Shipping, duties and tax are out of scope.

## How it works

1. `convertCircuitJsonToFabricationFiles` generates Gerbers, drill files, `bom.csv` and `pick_and_place.csv` with the same converters and options as the tscircuit.com fabrication export and `tsci export -f gerbers`.
2. `getQuoteInputsFromFabricationFiles` reads board size, layers, vias, holes, trace widths, paste openings and the BOM back out of those files. An existing fabrication export can be quoted directly with `quoteFabricationFiles`.
3. `lookupJlcParts` prices each BOM line from jlcsearch (unit price, stock, basic/preferred flag, footprint pads). Resistors and capacitors without a part number are matched by rating and package.
4. `estimateJlcpcbQuote` applies the fee rules in `lib/jlcpcb-price-table.ts`. It is pure, so real orders can be replayed against it.

The quote is deliberately computed from generated fabrication files rather than from Circuit JSON directly, so it sees exactly what JLCPCB receives and an existing fabrication export can be quoted too.

## Accuracy so far

| Case | Actual | Estimate |
|---|---|---|
| Live JLCPCB quote, 4-layer 144.5x82mm, 5 assembled, economic PCBA (end to end from fabrication files) | $348.43 | $363.79 (+4.4%) |
| Shipped order Y45 (fee rules replayed from the invoice) | $239.66 | within 3% |
| Shipped order Y63 (fee rules replayed from the invoice) | $125.30 | within 2% |

On the live quote every line matches JLCPCB except two: parts ($180.87 against $164.76) and SMT placement ($7.02 against $7.77). The parts gap is because jlcsearch only reports a single-piece price: JLCPCB's quantity price breaks are not applied and billed spares are estimated. The estimator already applies both when a part carries them, and with them the parts line matches to the cent; they need to be exposed by jlcsearch.

## Known limits

- Bare-PCB prices are fitted to very few data points. The 4-layer area price comes from one quote; 1-2 layer boards over 100mm, quantities above 5, 6+ layers, ENIG and all flex prices are heuristics with wide ranges.
- The 4-wire Kelvin test fee is inferred from supplement notices, three of which bundle duty/VAT.
- Standard PCBA rates come from JLCPCB's help page, not a live quote.
- Parts are priced from jlcsearch only, at single-piece prices with estimated spares, so the parts line carries a range and runs about 10% high on the one quote checked.
- It refuses instead of guessing: an unpriceable BOM line, a failed or malformed lookup, or a board with no price in the table throws. `unresolvedParts: "exclude"` quotes without the unpriceable lines and lists them.
- Lookups run one at a time, so a 73-part board takes about a minute.
- `circuit-json-to-gerber`, `circuit-json-to-bom-csv` and `circuit-json-to-pnp-csv` are now runtime dependencies.

## Testing

`bun test` (16 tests, no network), `bun run typecheck` and `bun run format:check` pass.

Updates the unit 322 manufacturing simulation from PR #1 in place, from a single job to the full motor controller line. It's the same page and the same `ManufacturingSimulation` core; nothing is added alongside the old version.

The operator now runs a batch of 30 NEMA17 motor controllers across four standing desks on the window wall: assembly, QC, pack-out and ship-ready. The batch ends with one sealed Amazon carton by the door. The 3D printers (Bambu P2S and H2S) and the label printer (Epson ET-2400) sit on their own benches on the east wall, and keep the line supplied with spacers and label sheets.

**The line**
- **Assembly:** load the motor, swap its 4 stock screws for long M3s through a 4 mm spacer and the PCB with the SKIL Twist 2.0, plug in the motor cable, rack it.
- **QC:** cradle, DATA and PWR USB-C, a spin test, then the ready rack.
- **Pack-out:** 7×4×3" mailer with pink foam, 2 USB-C cables, a 45 W charger and a 2×4" label.
- **Ship-ready:** 30 mailers into a 15×13×17" carton, flaps folded, taped, out by the door.
- **Printers:** the P2S and H2S print spacer plates (25 and 49 per plate). Finished plates go into a tub, which refills the assembly basket.
- **Labels:** the Epson prints AveneMark sheets; the operator carries them to pack-out.

Racks, a tote and the carton carry the batch from bench to bench. Every step is timed, and walking time is shown separately.

**Controller board.** It's modelled from the [imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller](https://tscircuit.com/imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller) v1.0.55 `circuit.json`:
- the 42.3 mm chamfered outline and 31 mm mounting holes;
- all 103 populated top-side parts at their placed positions;
- DATA and PWR USB-C on one edge, and the side-entry JST-PH J1, which takes the motor cable's PHR-4.

**Playing it**
- **Simulate:** a full batch of 30, or 1 motor from start to ship.
- **Jump to a bench:** start at any bench with the units already done up to it.
- **Equipment buttons:** "3D prints are ready" and "Labels printed".
- **Game mode keys:**
  - E runs a bench, and again pauses it.
  - R carries a part-filled rack or tote on to the next bench.
  - C carries on after a pause.
  - F picks up or puts back the screwdriver.
  - M toggles sound.
- **Collecting mid-run:** pause, walk to a blue circle at the label printer or a 3D printer, and E does that job now. When you walk away, he sets down what was in his hands, so nothing floats.
- **Sound:** synthesized with WebAudio, with no audio files. The screwdriver and the stepper follow the motion in the scene.
- **Operator:** a 6'2" figure with shaped limbs. He carries loads upright with both hands.

**Code**
- `lib/job`: the per-unit steps for each bench, slot-based containers, transfers and printer and label jobs. `bench-work.ts` picks the next work.
- `lib/simulation`: the headless core, game actions, line setup, pause parking, equipment circles and sound cues.
- `lib/models`: the standing desk, SKIL screwdriver, RP2040 board (from `rp2040-board-layout.ts`), Bambu printers, Epson, carton, mailer, racks, tote and JST and USB-C plugs.
- `lib/viewer/sound`: the WebAudio synthesis.
- `lib/models/folding-table.ts` is replaced by `standing-desk.ts`, and `lib/job/run-work-item.ts` by `bench-work.ts`.

**Assumptions to check**
- Table positions are placeholders in `lib/layout/station-layout.ts`.
- Gesture durations are placeholders, so the batch time of about 46½ min is not measured.
- Plate times are estimates, not slicer output.
- The 37 lb carton weight is an estimate; weigh a packed unit before ordering cartons.
- The buzzer chirp at QC assumes test firmware; the board ships with none.

**Validation**
- `bun test` passes: 23 tests. They cover:
  - the full 30-unit batch shipping in one sealed carton, and the 1-motor run;
  - jumping to each bench, and partial R carries;

description: Adds the unit 322 manufacturing simulation, laid out the way the tscircuit handbook bootstraps repos: bun with no lockfile, TypeScript in lib and tests, biome, the plop typechecktestformat workflows, and a React Cosmos site that Vercel builds with cosmos-export. body:
Adds the unit 322 manufacturing simulation, laid out the way the tscircuit handbook bootstraps repos: bun with no lockfile, TypeScript in `lib/` and `tests/`, biome, the plop typecheck/test/format workflows, and a React Cosmos site that Vercel builds with `cosmos-export`. It mirrors `drawing-viewer`.

A 6'2" operator walks the unit 322 floor and runs a 12-step job across three 6' tables. The job pulls a NEMA17 backface spacer from the P2S, swaps the motor's backface screws to mount the spacer and motor controller PCB, then folds a mailer box, adds foam inserts, packs the assembly and moves it to finished goods. Each step and walking time are clocked. Game mode lets you walk the operator (WASD), run the next step at a station (E) and pick up the screwdriver (F). The camera zooms down to the screws.

- `lib/simulation`: `ManufacturingSimulation`, a headless core with no DOM, so the job can be run and timed in tests.
- `lib/job`: the 12 steps, grouped by station. Each step is a generator built from the operator motions in `lib/tasks`.
- `lib/layout`, `lib/models`, `lib/world`, `lib/navigation`, `lib/operator`: floor plan, Three.js parts, bench contents, A* path finding and the operator rig with arm IK.
- `lib/viewer`: the React viewer (renderer, camera, HUD, keyboard and touch input).
- `pages/manufacturing-simulation.page.tsx`: the Cosmos fixture. `vercel.json` runs `bun run build:site` and serves `cosmos-export/`.

Table positions are placeholders until the real ones are known; they live in `lib/layout/station-layout.ts`. Gesture durations are also placeholders, so the ~75 s cycle time is not measured. The PCB, P2S, box and foam are simplified models. The spacer follows `backface-spacer-4mm.scad`.

Validation: `bun test` (8 tests: the full job completes with the assembly packed and timed, runs are deterministic, the operator is 6'2", navigation stays clear of obstacles, and the screwdriver and game-mode actions work), `bun run typecheck` and `bun run format:check` pass. `bun run build:site` builds, and I ran the exported site in headless Chromium through the full job, game mode, a phone-width view and dark mode.
