title: Rename the app from T3 Code to tscircuit desktop
description: The app is now called tscircuit desktop and carries tscircuits icon. It also has its own app ID, link scheme and data folders, so it can be installed beside T3 Code without sharing its data.
body:
The app is now called tscircuit desktop and carries tscircuit's icon. It also has its own app ID, link scheme and data folders, so it can be installed beside T3 Code without sharing its data.

![tscircuit desktop with the Circuit tab showing a schematic](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-desktop/blob/rebrand/docs/screenshot.png?raw=true)

## How the rename works

T3 Code writes its name in about 1,200 places and has no central constant for it. Carrying that as patches would conflict on every upstream bump, so the rename is a list of find-and-replace rules in `renames.json`:

- `setup` applies the rules to upstream first, then the overlay and patches. Patches are measured against the renamed code, so a rename never shows up as a patch.
- The rules are re-run from scratch on every bump, so they cannot conflict and they also cover text upstream adds later.
- Every rule states why it exists, and `setup` fails if a rule stops matching anything (upstream reworded what it was for).

30 rules rewrite 730 files. `export` also learned to save replaced binary files (the icons) whole in `overlay/`.

## What changed in the app

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Name | "tscircuit desktop" in window titles, dialogs, errors, settings and agent prompts |
| Icon | tscircuit's `ts` logo for the app, window and favicon; "tscircuit desktop" in the sidebar |
| Identity | App ID `com.tscircuit.desktop`, links `tscircuit-desktop://`, data in `~/.tscircuit-desktop` |
| Links | Download, releases, bug reports and the star prompt point at this repository |
| Analytics | Off by default. Upstream's default reports to T3 Code's analytics service |
| Old profiles | No import of settings from an installed T3 Code's older profile folders |

## Decisions worth a look

- **Lower case.** The name is written "tscircuit desktop" everywhere, including at the start of sentences. Say if you want "tscircuit Desktop".
- **Analytics are off, not redirected.** Turning them on with `T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED=true` still sends to T3 Code's service. The welcome screen and Settings now say usage data is off.
- **The privacy link** goes to a new Privacy section in the README, which says the app has no privacy policy of its own yet. That section lists what was checked, not a full audit.
- **Left alone on purpose:** the `t3` command, `T3CODE_` environment variables, and the names T3 Connect and T3 Chat (T3's own services; neither appears in this build's UI without their sign-in key).

## What was tested

- `npm test`: 15 script tests, 5 new (rules rewrite text and file names, a patch on a renamed file holds only our edit, a bump renames text upstream adds later, an unmatched rule stops setup, a replaced binary round-trips).
- `npm run check:app`: typecheck and lint of `apps/web`, 122 tests, unused-code check. The desktop app also typechecks.
- The app, run on Linux in development mode: title and welcome screen say tscircuit desktop, the page loads from `tscircuit-desktop-dev://`, the profile folder and launcher entry are the new ones, and the Circuit tab still renders the test project.
- T3 Code's own desktop, web and shared-package tests (about 7,900), used to find what the rules broke. That turned up three real problems, now fixed by rules: link-scheme patterns that no longer recognised the app's links, an encoded name in app links, and tool labels the chat no longer recognised.

## Not tested, or known to be unfinished

- **No installers.** Nothing has been packaged for macOS, Windows or Linux; the renamed IDs and file names have only run in development mode.
- **9 of T3 Code's own tests still fail**, all expected: 3 use the old name as sample data, 1 lists the old link scheme, 4 check links to T3 Code's repository, and 1 covers the profile import that is turned off. `check:app` does not run them. The list is in `docs/research.md`.
- **The server test suite did not finish** in the sandbox (25-minute limit). The six failures in the part that ran are from the sandbox, not the renames.
- **"Report a problem" still files to T3 Code's repository.** The built-in triage agent is written around their repo and needs rewriting before users get this.
- **The model list is still fetched from T3 Code's GitHub repository**, which is how the app learns about new models.

title: Build tscircuit desktop as an overlay on T3 Code
description: tscircuit desktop is T3 Code plus a small set of tscircuit changes. T3 Code lands about 180 commits a day, so this repo is not a fork: it holds only the difference and rebuilds the app from it.
body:
tscircuit desktop is [T3 Code](https://github.com/pingdotgg/t3code) plus a small set of tscircuit changes. T3 Code lands about 180 commits a day, so this repo is not a fork: it holds only the difference and rebuilds the app from it.

![The Circuit tab showing the schematic of led.tsx beside the chat](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-desktop/blob/t3code-overlay/docs/screenshot.png?raw=true)

## How it works

| Path | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `upstream.json` | The T3 Code commit we build on |
| `overlay/` | Files that exist only here, laid out as they sit in T3 Code |
| `patches/` | One patch per T3 Code file we change, each with a note saying why |
| `scripts/` | `setup` builds `.t3code/`, `export` saves work back, `bump` moves the pin |

Patches apply as three-way merges, so upstream edits elsewhere in a patched file merge on their own and real conflicts show up as ordinary conflict markers. `setup` refuses to rebuild over work that has not been exported.

## The tscircuit change: a Circuit tab

Circuits render in a right-panel tab of their own, next to Diff and Files. There is no address bar, no dev server, and none of RunFrame's File/View header: only its PCB, Schematic and 3D views.

- **Circuit** is in the panel's launcher and "+" menu (shortcut `C`). It renders the project's entry file.
- Opening any `.tsx` file, from the Files tab or a chat link, switches the Circuit tab to that file and names the tab after it. A link to a specific line still opens the source viewer.
- The tab re-renders when the agent finishes an edit, when a file is saved, and when the window regains focus.

It reads the project's files through T3 Code's file API and passes them to RunFrame's hosted viewer in a frame, with the viewer's file menu and run button off. That is six new files in `overlay/apps/web/src/tscircuit/` and five patches that add about 40 lines to T3 Code's own files.

This replaces the first version, a project action that ran `tsci dev` in the in-app browser.

## What was tested

- `npm test`: 10 tests of setup, export and bump against a stand-in upstream, including a conflicting bump and its resolution.
- A bump from a commit three weeks older than the pin (3,133 upstream commits) re-applied with no conflict. This was run with the first version's single patch, not the five current ones.
- `npm run check:app`: typecheck and lint of `apps/web`, 122 tests (11 new, 111 upstream tests of the right panel), and T3 Code's unused-code check.
- The patched desktop app, run on Linux: opened Circuit from the launcher; clicked `boards/led.tsx` in the Files tab and the Circuit tab took focus, renamed itself and drew that file's schematic; changed a resistor value on disk and the schematic updated within a few seconds.

## Not tested

- A real agent turn (no signed-in provider was available).
- The PCB tab, which needs WebGPU.
- Circuits that import npm packages. The viewer gets the project's own source files, not `node_modules`.
- The **Bump T3 Code** workflow, which has not run yet. It needs the repository setting that lets Actions create pull requests.

## Things to know before merging

- The viewer is loaded from `runframe.tscircuit.com`, so the Circuit tab needs internet. Bundling RunFrame clashed with the host app's dependencies and styles in an earlier prototype.
- Every `.tsx` opens in the Circuit tab, including ones that are not circuits.
- The app is still branded T3 Code.

The full list is in the README under "Known gaps".

title: Support string cadModel as a footprinter model on normal components
description: Enables the use of a string cadModel as a footprinter model for normal components, allowing for procedural generation of 3D models based on the cadModel string, independent of the PCB footprint.
body:
## Summary

`cadModel` already accepts a footprinter string in `@tscircuit/props` (`CadModelFootprinterString`), and the assembly elements already honor it, but on a normal component such as `<chip />` it threw `String cadModel not yet implemented`.

A string `cadModel` is now emitted as the `cad_component`'s `footprinter_string`, independently of the component's PCB footprint:

```tsx
<chip
  name="U1"
  footprint={<footprint>{/* exact pads */}</footprint>}
  cadModel="soic8"
/>
```

- A chip with a custom `<footprint>` gets a generated 3D model instead of a bounding box.
- When the footprint is also a footprinter string, the `cadModel` string takes precedence for the 3D model (`footprint="soic8" cadModel="tssop8"` keeps soic8 pads and renders a tssop8 body).
- Object, element and `null` `cadModel` values behave as before.

No props change is needed.

## Testing

- New: `chip-cad-model-footprinter-string.test.tsx` (with a simple-3d snapshot) and `chip-cad-model-footprinter-string-overrides-footprint.test.tsx`
- `bun test tests/components/normal-components tests/footprint` and `bun test tests/assembly` pass
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` reports nothing in the touched files

title: feat: implement finished panel size limits (#5067)
description: Implements finished panel size limits that enforce minimum and maximum dimensions for panels, affecting layout and error reporting.
body:
Implements **finished panel size limits** from https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/5067, using `minWidth`, `maxWidth`, `minHeight` and `maxHeight` from props 0.0.724 ([props#991](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/991)).

Following review ("you want to change the panel layout algorithm, not just error"), the limits now shape the grid layout of the root `<panel>`:

- **Maximums choose the grid.** When rows, columns and panel dimensions are left to the layout and the default grid would exceed `maxWidth` or `maxHeight`, `Subpanel.doInitialPanelBoardLayout` tries each column count and keeps the smallest grid that fits. `Panel._getMaxGridSize` subtracts the edge padding from the limits; subpanels have no limits.
- **Minimums grow the panel.** An auto-sized panel smaller than `minWidth` or `minHeight` grows to it in `Panel._updatePanelDimensions`, keeping its boards centred.
- **Errors only when impossible.** A limit that no layout can meet, or that explicit dimensions break, is still reported as a `pcb_panelization_placement_error`, for example "Panel width 40 mm exceeds the maximum width 20 mm".
- Limits on a nested `<subpanel>` throw "Panel size limits must be configured on the root <panel>".

In the repro, the four boards become one column in a 24 × 100 mm panel with no errors; the fix updates the repro's PCB snapshot and inline snapshot. A new test covers a board wider than `maxWidth`. Panels without size limits lay out exactly as before (existing snapshots unchanged).

Props docs are updated to match in https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/1000 (they said the limits were validation only).

Validation: the repro, the new test and all 62 test files that render `<panel>`/`<subpanel>` pass (96 pass, 2 existing skips); full typecheck passes.

title: feat: V-score panel tabs with vScore (#5067)
description: Implements V-scored panel tabs that replace mouse bites with score lines along the board edge for panels using tab-routing and vScore.
body:
Implements **V-scored panel tabs** from https://github.com/tscircuit/core/issues/5067, using the published `vScore` boolean from props 0.0.724 ([props#990](https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/990)).

When a `<panel>` or `<subpanel>` uses `panelizationMethod="tab-routing"` with `vScore`, each tab gets one score line along the board edge, spanning the tab, exactly where its mouse bites would otherwise be drilled:

- `generatePanelTabsAndMouseBites` takes a `vScore` option and returns `vScoreLines` (one two-point route per tab) alongside the tab cutouts and mouse-bite holes.
- `Subpanel` writes each line as a panel-owned `pcb_fabrication_note_path` on the top fabrication layer, 0.1 mm wide (named `V_SCORE_LINE_LAYER` and `V_SCORE_LINE_STROKE_WIDTH`).
- Props already turns off omitted `mouseBites` when `vScore` is set, so no holes are drilled. Panels without `vScore` are unchanged.
- Curved board outlines (the continuous routed-slot fallback) cannot be V-scored and throw `V-scored panel tabs require straight board edges`.

This replaces the earlier `panelizationMethod="v_score"` design (full-span score lines across zero-gap panels), which review rejected. Its annotation generator, rectangular bounds helper and validation test are removed.

The fix updates the repro's same snapshot: the 16 tab gaps now carry score lines (thin fabrication-note lines on the board edge). The repro's inline snapshot changes from `0` to `16` score lines with no holes, and a new test checks the full curved-outline error with an inline snapshot.

Validation with published props 0.0.724: the repro, the new test and all 62 test files that render `<panel>`/`<subpanel>` pass (95 pass, 2 existing skips, 439 assertions); full typecheck and formatting pass.

Adds `tscircuit.com/desktop` for the desktop app, laid out like `/enterprise`, and links it from the Product menu.

## What is on the page

- What the app is, in two paragraphs.
- **Download.** The button points at the `.dmg` of the newest published release of `tscircuit/tscircuit-desktop`, looked up from GitHub in the browser the way `/enterprise` does it. The `.zip` is under "Other download formats". If the lookup fails the button goes to the releases page.
- **Only an Apple silicon macOS build exists.** Visitors on Windows or Linux get "Not available for Windows yet" and the Mac download as a secondary button, instead of a primary button for an installer they cannot run.
- **The app is not signed by Apple yet**, so the page says how to open it the first time (Privacy & Security → Open Anyway).
- A screenshot, then three feature cards.

Also: `desktop` is reserved as a top-level route and the server renders this page's title and description for it, `/desktop` is in the sitemap, and the Product menu has a "tscircuit Desktop" entry above Enterprise.

## About the screenshot

It is the PCB view of `imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller` in the app, as asked. Three things to know before it goes live:

- **The released app cannot open that project yet.** It needed two changes I made only in my local build: the Circuit tab's size limits raised (the project has a 2 MB routing file; the app stops at 1 MB per file and 2 MB in total), and the eval worker from tscircuit 0.0.3102, which the project pins. On the app's bundled tscircuit the project stops in its own schematic check. So the picture is a real render in the app's interface, but not one today's download reproduces.
- **It was taken in a development build on Linux**, so there is no macOS window frame, and no agent was signed in: the composer reads "Enable a provider in Settings to send a message".
- A screenshot from a signed-in session on a Mac would be better. I can retake it once the app opens this project out of the box.

## Testing

- `bun test`: the new `desktop-page-seo` test and the existing enterprise one pass. I could not run the rest: `bun install` cannot fetch this repo's GitHub-hosted dependencies from my sandbox.
- `tsc --noEmit`: no errors in the changed files. The only errors are the missing modules from those dependencies.
- `biome format` is clean on the changed files.
- I opened `/desktop` on this PR's Vercel preview at 1280 px as a Mac visitor. The page, header and footer render, and the button points at the live newest release (`v0.1.10`).
- Locally I rendered the page by itself (header and footer stubbed out, for the same reason as above) at 375 px as a Windows visitor with the release lookup mocked: the "Not available for Windows yet" wording shows and nothing overflows.
- `playwright-tests/desktop-page.spec.ts` is new and **has not been run**. `enterprise-page.spec.ts` now expects six Product links; its `product-menu` and `product-mobile` snapshots need "update snapshots".

The landing page's menu link is tscircuit/tscircuit.com-landing#78; merge this one first.

Cannot pull with rebase due to unstaged changes in the following files:
 - lib/hooks/styles.generated.ts

#6289 added the class `[&>[role=tabpanel]]:!rf-mt-0`. Tailwind emits two rules for it, the variant and a plain `.!rf-mt-0`. title: Add useRunFrameController, and let a host hide the header and follow renders
description: tscircuit desktop frames RunFrame and is getting its own view tabs (Source, PCB, Schematic, 3D, System, Assembly) in the apps style. For that the page around RunFrame needs three things RunFrame did not offer: remove RunFrames header, choose the tab from outside, and know what a circuit contains. The app also wants to frame the RunFrame that the tscircuit package ships, in place of runframe.tscircuit.comiframe.html, so the standalone bundle learns to take its props the same way.
body:
tscircuit desktop frames RunFrame and is getting its own view tabs (Source, PCB, Schematic, 3D, System, Assembly) in the app's style. For that the page around RunFrame needs three things RunFrame did not offer: remove RunFrame's header, choose the tab from outside, and know what a circuit contains. The app also wants to frame the RunFrame that the `tscircuit` package ships, in place of `runframe.tscircuit.com/iframe.html`, so the standalone bundle learns to take its props the same way.

## What changes

**`useRunFrameController`**, in the shape of `usePcbViewerController` and `useSchematicViewerController`:

```tsx
const { controller, activeTab, setActiveTab, isRunning, circuitJsonElementCounts, errorMessage } =
  useRunFrameController()

<RunFrame fsMap={fsMap} controller={controller} showHeader={false} />
```

`setActiveTab` works before RunFrame mounts. `activeTab` follows RunFrame when it switches by itself (to `errors` after a run throws, and back). `RunFrameWithIframe` takes the same `controller`. The hook is built on the three pieces below, which a host can also use directly, for example over `postMessage` without the package.

**`showHeader`** (default `true`). `false` removes the whole header: run button, file menu, render status and tabs.

**`activeTab`**. Picks the tab. While it is set, RunFrame does not switch tabs on its own. A switch it would have made (to `errors` after a failed run, back to the previous tab after a good one, "view in schematic") is reported through `onActiveTabChange` and the host decides whether to follow. Without `activeTab`, nothing changes.

**Events from the iframe to its parent.** Until now only `error` was sent.

| Event | Sent when | Fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `render_started` | A run begins | |
| `circuit_json_changed` | First Circuit JSON of a run, and the final one | `circuit_json_element_counts` |
| `render_finished` | A run rendered to the end | `circuit_json_element_counts` |
| `run_completed` | A run ends, rendered or thrown | `has_execution_error`, `error_count` |
| `active_tab_changed` | The tab changes, or RunFrame asks for one | `tab` |

`circuit_json_element_counts` is a count of elements by type (`{ "pcb_board": 1, "system_block_page": 1 }`). It is enough for a host to tell which views have something to show, and far smaller than the Circuit JSON.

**Capabilities in the ready message.** `runframe_ready_to_receive` now carries `runframe_capabilities: ["show_header", "active_tab", "render_events"]`, so a host can tell an older deployment from a newer one.

**The standalone bundle can be driven by its parent.** `dist/standalone.min.js` (shipped in `tscircuit` as `dist/browser.min.js`) renders `RunFrameWithApi` or a static preview. With `window.TSCIRCUIT_USE_RUNFRAME_PROPS_FROM_PARENT = true` set before it loads, it instead does what `iframe.html` does: announces `runframe_ready_to_receive`, takes its props from `runframe_props_changed` messages and reports the events above. Both now render one new component, `RunFrameInIframe`, so the hosted embed and the packaged bundle cannot drift apart. Without the flag the standalone bundle behaves as before.

## One fix along the way

The README tells hosts to check `event.data.runframe_type === "runframe_event"`, but the iframe only ever sent `type: "runframe_event"`. Events now carry both fields, so code written from the README starts working and code that reads `type` keeps working.

## For the reviewer

- Most of the `CircuitJsonPreview.tsx` diff is the header being indented one level inside `{showHeader && (…)}`. With whitespace hidden the change is about 20 lines.
- In `RunFrame.tsx`, the tab used for analytics and render-log timings is now the host's tab when one is set.

## Testing

- New `tests/run-frame-controller.test.tsx`: a host using the hook with a real `RunFrame` and preview (static Circuit JSON, so no worker). It gets the element counts, switches tabs, lands on `errors` when the file stops parsing and returns to the tab it left when it parses again, and the host's own callbacks still fire.

- New `tests/host-controlled-tabs.test.tsx`: the header is gone with `showHeader: false`, `activeTab` wins over a tab stored from an earlier visit, a failed run asks for `errors` without switching, a later good run asks for the tab it left, and an unknown tab is ignored.
- New `tests/get-circuit-json-element-counts1.test.ts` and `…2.test.ts`.
- These plus the existing tab tests (system view, extra tabs, solver tab switching, render status, schematic-to-PCB navigation) pass here and in CI.
- `bunx tsc --noEmit` and `biome format` are clean. I could not install `circuit-json-to-altium` in my sandbox (GitHub tarball blocked), so anything that imports it was not typechecked or run here.
- New `tests/run-frame-in-iframe.test.tsx`: a parent window and `RunFrameInIframe` talking over real `message` events. It gets the ready message with its capabilities, sends files and a tab, and receives the render events.
- `RunFrameWithIframe` with a controller is typechecked but has no test of its own.
- The bundles themselves (`build:iframe`, `build:standalone`) were not built locally. The `iframe.min.js` that Vercel built for this PR is what tscircuit/tscircuit-desktop#5 bundles and was run with: PCB, schematic, 3D, system and assembly views, a file with a syntax error, and tab changes from the host. The standalone bundle's new mode has only the test above behind it; it was not run in a browser.

title: Warn in tsci import when a chip has no 3D model
description: Adds a warning in the tsci import process when a chip lacks a 3D model, suggesting a footprinter model instead.
body:
## Summary

`tsci import` now warns when the imported chip has no 3D model, and recommends giving it a footprinter model:

```
Warning: No 3D model is available for this part.
  Give the chip a footprinter model in imports/AP2127K_2_8TRG1.tsx:
    cadModel="sot25_w2.6mm_pl1mm_pin1location(leftside,bottom)"
  "sot25_w2.6mm_pl1mm_pin1location(leftside,bottom)" is the closest footprinter match (99.11% copper IoU).
  Docs: https://docs.tscircuit.com/footprints/footprinter-strings
```

`importComponentFromJlcpcb` now returns this as metadata, and the CLI warning reads it:

```ts
model3d:
  | { isAvailable: true; source: "cad-model" }
  | { isAvailable: true; source: "footprinter-string"; footprinterString: string }
  | { isAvailable: false; closestFootprinter?: FootprinterDiscoveryCandidate }
```

- **Available:** the supplier part has an OBJ/STEP model, or the footprint was converted to a footprinter string (every footprinter string is assumed to have a generated 3D model).
- **Not available:** an exact `<footprint>` with no supplier model. `closestFootprinter` is the low-accuracy candidate the default footprint conversion already computed (no minimum IoU is applied); no extra footprinter discovery runs. With `--use-exact-footprint`, or when nothing matches, the warning shows a generic `soic8` example.
- **Output:** `console.warn` (stderr), yellow.
- **Not covered:** `TSCIRCUIT_STANDALONE=1` imports that write the datasheet API's `generated_tsx` directly, since that response carries no 3D model metadata.

## Depends on tscircuit/core#5483

The recommended `cadModel="<footprinter string>"` form throws `String cadModel not yet implemented` on a chip in released core. tscircuit/core#5483 (merged) implements it; this should merge after that is released.

## Testing

- New `tests/lib/import/import-missing-3d-model-warning.test.ts` (7 tests) passes, covering the metadata for each case and the warning
- The `runCommand`-based tests in `tests/cli/import` could not run in my sandbox (`Failed to listen at ::`), with or without this change, so they need CI

title: Implement tsci quote estimate with the JLCPCB quote estimator
description: The tsci quote estimate command now produces a real JLCPCB estimate instead of a placeholder, providing detailed cost breakdowns for PCB fabrication, assembly, shipping, and taxes based on user-defined parameters.
body:
## Summary

`tsci quote estimate` now produces a real JLCPCB estimate instead of the placeholder from #5759, using [`@tscircuit/circuit-json-to-jlcpcb-quote`](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-jlcpcb-quote).

```
tsci quote estimate board.circuit.tsx --quantity 5 --assembled 2
```

```
                                                           Total                   Per board
  PCB fabrication, 5 boards                                $4.05                 $0.81 / PCB
  Additional fees (1)                                      $0.10     $0.05 / assembled board
  Assembly, Economic PCBA                                 $11.16     $5.58 / assembled board
  Parts                                                    $0.01     $0.01 / assembled board
  Shipping, DHL Express (DDP) (0.648kg)                   $27.89    $13.95 / assembled board
  Import duties and taxes (35% of merchandise)             $5.36     $2.68 / assembled board
  Duty and tax disbursement fee                            $7.52     $3.76 / assembled board
  Sales tax (8.625% of merchandise)                        $1.32     $0.66 / assembled board
  ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
  Grand total                                             $57.41    $28.71 / assembled board
```

*(Output for a 20×20 mm test board with one resistor and one capacitor; the full output continues with the details below the table.)*

## How it works

- The file is resolved like other commands (`getEntrypoint`). Circuit JSON is read as is; a source file goes through `getOrGenerateCircuitJson`, reusing a current `tsci build`.
- The quote package converts the circuit JSON to the same fabrication files `tsci export -f gerbers` writes (same converters and options) and quotes from those. It prices parts from jlcsearch and shows lookup progress on a terminal.
- Output is the summary table, then details: fabrication, additional fees with their reasons, Economic and Standard PCBA side by side, DHL and UPS, and the BOM. `--json` prints the whole quote object to stdout; messages go to stderr.
- Parts that cannot be priced are left out and listed in the warnings.

## Options

- **Kept:** `--assembly` / `--no-assembly`, `--quantity` and `--json` behave as before.
- **New:**
  - `--assembled <count>`: PCBs to assemble, at most `--quantity`. Default 2, or `--quantity` if lower. More is refused before any lookup.
  - `--pcba auto|economic|standard`: default `auto`, which is Economic when the board allows it.
  - `--finish hasl_lead_free|hasl_leaded|enig`: default lead-free HASL.
  - `--carrier dhl|ups`: default DHL.
  - `--shipping-cost <usd>` and `--weight <kg>`: exact figures from JLCPCB's checkout; estimated when omitted.

`tsci quote create` is unchanged and still a placeholder.

## Dependency

`@tscircuit/circuit-json-to-jlcpcb-quote` 0.0.4 from jscdn, like the other `@tscircuit` analysis packages. It brings its own `@types/papaparse`; the package ships TypeScript source, so the CLI type check reads it.

The grand total assumes delivery to the US. The 35% import duty is for US deliveries and the default sales tax rate is tscircuit's address. The output says so under the summary table.

## Testing

`tests/cli/quote/quote.test.ts` is rewritten:

- **Offline quote:** a bare-board quote of a generated 20×20 mm board with `--json`; no part lookups, so it runs offline. Checks the order, the board read from the files, a $4.05 fabrication total and the summary.
- **Text output:** the table with `--quantity 10 --carrier ups --shipping-cost 20`.
- **Quantity rule:** more assembled boards than PCBs is refused.
- **Option validation:** for every new option.
- **`quote create`:** still a placeholder.

All 6 pass locally against the published 0.0.4. The error messages, the `quote create` placeholder output, the summary table and the destination note are inline snapshots. This sandbox has no IPv6, which every `getCliTestFixture` test needs, so I ran them with a preload that makes `get-port` listen on IPv4; CI needs no such shim. `biome format` is clean and the new files typecheck. The only `tsc` errors locally are the `github:` dependencies the sandbox cannot download.

I also ran it with assembly against the live jlcsearch: the output above, and a 73-part board in an earlier session. Those runs are not part of the tests, which stay offline.

title: Speed up exact node repair obstacle checks
description: Optimizes the exact distance calculations for node repair by caching and reusing spatial queries, significantly reducing compute time during autorouting.
body:
Candidate evaluation repeatedly computes exact distances from every trace segment to every obstacle, even when their bounding boxes cannot meet clearance. In the parallel autorouter benchmark, a single 18-route node with 3,043 points and 7,296 candidate checks accounts for 97% of worker compute time, preventing node-level parallelism from scaling.

Reject clearly separated copper/obstacle bounding boxes with conservative floating-point padding before exact distance calculations. Cache bounds, baseline obstacle clearances, route net identities, and boundary checks for unchanged geometry. Reuse identical spatial-index query boxes with a bounded hit cache, and visit only route pairs involving the changed route, in original order. The original conflict iteration, candidate ordering, scores, and acceptance checks are retained.

Validation: 18 focused clearance tests pass, including a saved original-output hash and full statistics for the 7,296-candidate node, three original dataset18 repair results, fixed copper, via layers, net identity, and spatial-index ordering and reuse of unchanged queries with invalidation on changed bounds or clearance. TypeScript checking passes. The full suite was attempted: 25 tests pass and 69 fail because dataset01 assets are absent or existing graphics snapshots differ; no snapshots were updated.

This supports the parallel-repair work in https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/pull/3059. The final autorouter integration benchmark on 5 srj18 boards (3 repetitions in rotated order, 16 effective CPUs, affinity 0–15, unlimited cgroup quota) measured original sequential repair at 28.972s and 8-worker repair at 6.813s including setup: **4.25× faster**, or **4.80× for solving alone**. The optimized one-worker control took 8.398s including setup. These are combined integration gains from the exact kernel optimizations, omitted unused wrapper diagnostics, and node parallelism; going from 1 to 8 workers contributed 1.27× to solve time. Every output hash and repair statistic matched the original sequential reference.

[Benchmark and raw results](https://github.com/tscircuit/tscircuit-autorouter/actions/runs/38477375845), measured with this dependency at `1981ac8d3547772cb4b0267f26c7a0c2fd4dea09`.

The [two-record fixture](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-webgpu/blob/75b88bba08b8ede3938116498616e4622b28798b/tests/fixtures/classic-f1-j6-ground.ts) uses the original endpoints, 0.15 mm width, and flags of the 15.2 mm top-layer GND trace beside the J6 LCD connector (`pcb_trace_external_163`). Keep pour-covered geometry in the draw mesh and use the existing pour-opacity uniform to control its visibility. Selected X-Ray traces remain visible. This supersedes the initial polygon-clipping approach for this visibility fix.

title: Ship @types/papaparse, state the tax destination, fix one-column CSVs
description: Moves typespapaparse to dependencies, adds tax destination details to quotes, and fixes parsing for one-column CSVs.
body:
## Summary

Follow-ups from the review of tscircuit/cli#5771.

- **`@types/papaparse` moves to `dependencies`.** The package ships TypeScript source, and `lib/fabrication-files/parse-csv-rows.ts` imports `papaparse`, so any project that type-checks it needs the types. The CLI had to add `@types/papaparse` itself; with this it can drop it.
- **The quote states which destination its taxes are for.** The grand total applies a 35% import duty and an 8.625% sales tax, which are only right for delivery to the US, and the sales tax only for tscircuit's address. The new `quote.destination` field (`country`, `importTaxRate`, `salesTaxRate`, `isDefaultSalesTaxRate`, `note`) records that. The text output and the quote page print the note under the grand total:
  > Shipping and taxes assume delivery to the United States with duties paid: 35% import duties and 8.625% sales tax (the rate on tscircuit's orders; it depends on the delivery address). Other destinations are not modelled.

  `salesTaxRate` already lets a caller price another US address. Other countries would need their own duty and shipping data, which we don't have yet.
- **Fabrication CSVs are read as comma-separated.** Papaparse's delimiter detection fails on a one-column file, which the BOM reader treated as fatal. That broke `a smaller exempt drill does not hide a chargeable via`, the test added in #6, which fails on `main` today.

## Release note

The 0.0.3 publish succeeded, but its last step, enabling auto-merge on the version-bump PR, fails because auto-merge is not allowed in this repo. So #7 ("bump version to v0.0.3") is still open and `package.json` still says 0.0.2. Merging #7, or allowing auto-merge, lets the next release go out cleanly as 0.0.4 for the CLI to pick up.

## Testing

- `bun test`: 41 pass, including the test from #6.
- `bun run typecheck` and `bun run format:check` are clean.
- New inline snapshots: `quote.destination` and its note for the default and an explicit sales tax rate. The quote snapshot is updated for the new field.

title: Fix publishing: install dependencies before configuring GitHub Packages
description: Fixes the GitHub Packages publishing failure by installing dependencies before configuring the registry, allowing the CLI integration to function correctly.
body:
## Summary

Nothing has been published since 0.0.2: the "Publish to GitHub Packages" job has failed on every merge (#2, #3, #4) at `bun install --frozen-lockfile` with errors like:

```
error: GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@tscircuit%2fcapacity-autorouter - 401
error: GET https://npm.pkg.github.com/@tscircuit%2fcore - 404
```

`actions/setup-node` with `scope: "@tscircuit"` points every `@tscircuit/*` package at GitHub Packages, and it ran before the install. The scaffold had no `@tscircuit` dependencies, but the estimator does: `circuit-json-to-gerber` and the BOM and pick-and-place converters pull public `@tscircuit/*` packages from npm.

This installs dependencies first and configures the registry afterwards, only for `pver release`, which is how `circuit-json-to-drawing` publishes. `--frozen-lockfile` is dropped because `bun.lock` is git-ignored here.

The CLI integration needs a published version to depend on, so this unblocks it.

## Testing

Only the workflow changes. The install step is the same `bun install` that the test, typecheck and format workflows already run successfully on every push.

Makes the unit 322 simulation usable on phones and tablets. This follows tscircuit/manufacturing-simulation#3, which merged before this commit was pushed.

**Layout on touch screens** (detected by `pointer: coarse`)
- Both panels start folded as small tabs at the top. Tapping one opens it as a sheet, and only one opens at a time. The sheet uses the full height in landscape.

**Controls**
- **Walk stick (game mode):** touching anywhere on the left half of the screen brings up a stick under the thumb. It disappears when the thumb lifts. While a menu is open the stick is off, and a tap shows "Close the menu to walk".
- **Camera:** the right half drags the camera, and pinch zooms.
- **Buttons, bottom-right:** a big E, plus R, C and F when they're available, and a camera button that cycles Follow, Close-up and Room.

**Also fixed:** on narrow screens the panels never folded at startup. The fold ran before the panels had rendered.

**Code**
- `lib/viewer/hud/touch-controls.tsx`: the floating stick zone, the menu message and the action buttons.
- `lib/viewer/hud/status-bar.tsx`: prompts as buttons (`getPromptActions` is shared with the touch buttons), and touch hints.
- `lib/viewer/manufacturing-simulation-viewer.tsx`: the `touch` class, panel folding and one-at-a-time sheets, the rotate tip and the camera cycle.
- `lib/viewer/viewer-styles.ts`: the touch layout, with safe-area insets for notched phones.

**Validation**
- `bun test` (24 tests), `bun run typecheck`, `bun run format:check` and `bun run build:site` pass.

title: Sign releases with tscircuit's Developer ID and notarize them
description: This PR changes the release process by signing the app with tscircuits Developer ID and notarizing it, allowing macOS to open downloaded copies without user intervention.
body:
Releases were signed ad hoc, so macOS refused to open a downloaded copy until you chose **Open Anyway**. This signs the app with tscircuit's Developer ID and has Apple notarize it, using the same secrets and the same approach as `tscircuit-standalone`.

## What changes

- **`scripts/sign-macos.sh`**, adapted from tscircuit-standalone's script of the same name: temporary keychain, Developer ID Application identity for team `WUQ9WUY75Z`, hardened runtime and secure timestamp, notarization with the App Store Connect key, stapling, Gatekeeper checks, and cleanup that removes the keychain. It never falls back to ad hoc signing.
- An Electron app is a bundle of bundles, so unlike the single `tsci` binary it is signed from the inside out: the 28 loose program files (native modules, `rg`, `spawn-helper`, …), then the four frameworks and four helper apps, then the app itself.
- The app is notarized and stapled first; the `.zip` and `.dmg` are then made from the stapled app, and the `.dmg` is signed, notarized and stapled too. That is two submissions to Apple per build.
- **`scripts/macos-entitlements.plist`**: the three entitlements tscircuit-standalone uses (JIT, unsigned executable memory, no library validation) plus camera and microphone, which T3 Code's own signed builds claim so that commands run in the app's terminals are not silently denied them.
- **Release workflow**: the ad hoc step becomes "Sign, notarize and package". A pull request from a fork (no secrets) still gets an ad hoc build. A push to `main` without the secrets fails instead of publishing an unsigned app. Job timeout goes from 60 to 90 minutes to leave room for Apple.
- The release notes and README no longer say the app is unsigned.

T3 Code's packaging script can sign, but only when its passkey sign-in is configured (provisioning profile, sign-in domain), which this app does not use. So the finished app is signed in the workflow and the packaging script is left alone.

## Not in this PR

- **Automatic updates.** Signing was the blocker, but the app is still built without an update feed. Turning it on also needs a `latest-mac.yml` written for the signed zip.
- The "not signed yet" sentence on tscircuit.com/desktop, which goes in its own PR once a signed release exists.

## Not ready to merge: the secrets are not in this repository yet

This PR's build (run 43572480911) received **empty** values for all five secrets: `MACOS_CERTIFICATE_P12_BASE64`, `MACOS_CERTIFICATE_PASSWORD`, `APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_P8_BASE64`, `APPLE_NOTARY_KEY_ID`, `APPLE_NOTARY_ISSUER_ID`. It is a same-repository pull request, so they would have been passed if tscircuit-desktop could see them. They are either repository secrets of tscircuit-standalone, or organization secrets not shared with this repository.

So the green check here only shows the ad hoc fallback. **The Developer ID path has not run against Apple yet**, and merging now would make the next release fail (by design: no unsigned release). Once the five secrets are visible to this repository, re-run the build; the signing and notarization then run on this PR.

## Checks so far

- Dry run of the script against the v0.1.10 app with stand-ins for Apple's tools, to check the order and arguments of every `codesign` call; `shellcheck` clean; `npm test` passes.
- Not yet checked: real signing, notarization (Apple may object to individual files inside the app), stapling and Gatekeeper.

One thing to expect after installing a signed build over an unsigned one: macOS may ask once to let the app use its saved keychain items, because the app's signature changed. With a stable Developer ID that should not come back on later updates.

body:
Stacked on #4 (the `t3` command rename). Merge that first; this one then shows only its own changes against `main`.

## What changes

**The Circuit tab has its own row of views**, in the app's style, where RunFrame's header was:

**Source · PCB · Schematic · 3D · System · Assembly**

- **Source** is first and shows the file's text with the app's read-only viewer.
- **RunFrame's header is gone.** The app tells RunFrame which view to draw; RunFrame reports what the rendered circuit contains.
- **Views with nothing in them are greyed out.** A system-only file greys out PCB, 3D and Assembly; a board without `systemblock` elements greys out System. When a file is first opened on an empty view, the app moves to the first view that has something.
- **Clicking a greyed-out view opens a dialog** with a short TSX example of what to add, and an **Add to prompt** button. For System it adds "Add TSX systemblock elements to populate the System view".
- **A file that does not run** gets an error tab with RunFrame's error list. Every view is greyed out, and their dialog shows the error with a "Fix this error in …" prompt. Once the file runs, the tab returns to the view it left.

**The viewer is bundled into the app.** Nothing is loaded from `runframe.tscircuit.com` or a CDN to draw a circuit.

- `viewer.json` names what to bundle, and `setup` downloads it and checks its hashes: the `tscircuit` package, whose `dist/browser.min.js` is RunFrame with its eval worker inside, and `manifold-3d` for the 3D view. They are generated, not committed, like the skill. The app grows by about 64 MB.
- RunFrame's own usage analytics (PostHog) are turned off in the bundled viewer, as the app's are, and RunFrame no longer asks jsDelivr which eval version is newest.

## It needs tscircuit 0.0.3179 or newer

The row of views needs a RunFrame that the page around it can drive. tscircuit/runframe#6289 added that and 0.0.3179 is the first `tscircuit` release with it. `viewer.json` takes `"tscircuit": "latest"` at build time, and `setup` stops with a clear message if it is given a version that is too old.

## Where the viewer runs

RunFrame runs the project's code, so it must not share the app's origin: the app's session can start agents and terminals. The hosted viewer was on another site; a bundled one is not, so:

- **In the desktop app** the viewer is served on a host of its own, `tscircuit-desktop://viewer`. Checked from inside the frame: the app's page and storage are out of reach, fetching the app's files is refused, and so are requests to the local server.
- **In a browser** (`tscircuit-desktop` from a terminal) there is no second origin, so the frame is sandboxed without one. **The PCB view does not draw there**: it needs WebGPU in a worker, which a frame without an origin does not get. The other views work.

One patch to T3 Code's protocol handler serves that host, with a content security policy that allows the eval RunFrame needs.

## Decisions for you

- **The app's copy of tscircuit is used, not the project's.** A project with its own `tscircuit` in `node_modules` is still rendered with the version the app was built with. This matters for projects that pin an older tscircuit: `imrishabh18/rp2040-motor-controller` (pinned to 0.0.3102) stops in its own schematic check on the bundled version, and renders when given 0.0.3102's worker. Using the project's version is a follow-up, not part of this PR.
- **RunFrame's analytics are off** in the app. They are yours, so flip `TSCIRCUIT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` in `frame.html` if you want them. The README's privacy section says they are off.
- **Source is read-only.** It reuses the app's lightweight viewer. The full editor would need the file panel's larger component.
- **An error tab was added** beyond the six views you listed. Without RunFrame's header there was nowhere else for a syntax error to show.

## Still fetched from the web

- **Part lookups** for the components a circuit uses (`jlcsearch.tscircuit.com`, `easyeda.com`), and packages a circuit imports. This is tscircuit rendering, not the viewer loading itself.
- **Fonts for 3D text** (three files from jsDelivr), and `occt-import-js` if a board has a STEP model. RunFrame has a `TSCIRCUIT_JSCDN_BASE_URL` setting that would let these be bundled too; the font index does not go through it.

## Testing

- `npm run check:app`: typecheck of the three apps, lint, 162 tests, unused-code check. `npm test`: 19 script tests, one new, which builds the viewer from a fake registry and a pinned file and checks a changed file or a too-old RunFrame stops the build.

Every request was logged; none went to `runframe.tscircuit.com`, none fetched the worker or manifold-3d, and none went to PostHog. - A clean `setup` from this branch applies all 20 patches and bundles the viewer.

title: Rename the t3 command to tscircuit-desktop and stop sharing names with T3 Code
description: Renames the command from t3 to tscircuit-desktop to avoid conflicts with T3 Code, ensuring separate environment variables, project files, and git references for the two applications.
body:
On a machine that also has T3 Code, tscircuit desktop still used several of T3 Code's names. The worst one: on first launch the app links its command into `~/.local/bin` as `t3`, which takes the name of T3 Code's own command.

## What is separate now

| | tscircuit desktop | T3 Code |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Command | `tscircuit-desktop` | `t3` |
| Environment variables | `TSCIRCUIT_DESKTOP_…` | `T3CODE_…` |
| Project file | `tscircuit-desktop.json` | `t3.json` |
| Branches it creates | `tscircuit/…` | `t3/…`, `t3code/…` |
| Hidden git refs (checkpoints) | `refs/tscircuit-desktop/…` | `refs/t3/…`, `refs/t3code/…` |
| Compile cache folder | `tscircuit-desktop` | `t3code` |
| Background service | `tscircuit-desktop.service` | `t3code.service` |

The data folder, app ID and link scheme were already separate. All of this is 25 new rules in `renames.json`, each with its reason.

## Moving an existing install

Builds up to 0.1.3 already linked `t3`. A new module, `apps/desktop/src/tscircuit/legacyT3Command.ts`, runs at startup:

- It removes a `t3` link only when the link leads to this app's own old launcher and that launcher carries this app's marker. T3 Code's `t3` leads to `~/.t3` and is never touched.
- An install that had the command gets `tscircuit-desktop` linked in its place. If that cannot be done yet (no shell PATH on this launch), it is tried again on the next launch.

## What changes for someone on 0.1.3

- `t3` in a terminal stops being this app; `tscircuit-desktop` replaces it.
- Checkpoints that 0.1.3 made stay under `refs/t3/` in the project, so threads from that build cannot be rolled back to them.
- A `t3.json` written by 0.1.3 is no longer read. Rename it to `tscircuit-desktop.json`.
- `T3CODE_TELEMETRY_ENABLED` is now `TSCIRCUIT_DESKTOP_TELEMETRY_ENABLED`.

## Not separate yet

- A Linux package would still install a binary named `t3code`. No Linux package is built.
- Connecting to another machine over SSH installs T3's server there, under T3 Code's names.
- Agents still see the app's tools as `t3-code`, and both apps use the same `branch.<name>.t3-…` git config keys.

## Also in this PR

- The Release workflow now builds pull requests that change the app (rules, overlay, patches, branding, scripts), not only ones that change the workflow. It still publishes only from `main`.
- The telemetry patch was re-saved, because its lines now contain the renamed variable.

## Testing

- `npm run check:app`: typecheck of the three apps, lint, 132 tests (6 new, for the move from `t3`), unused-code check.
- `npm test`: 18 script tests.
- T3 Code's own test of the command link fails on names it writes by hand (`"bin", "t3"`). With those changed in a scratch copy, 7 of its 8 failures pass; the eighth matches `t3.cmd` in its own regular expression. Similar failures in the server's installer tests were read, not re-run. Details are in `docs/research.md`.
- Not yet run on a Mac. The build from this PR is the first chance to.

title: Automatic releases, bundled tscircuit skill, plain name and a full-size icon
description: Four changes that take tscircuit desktop from runs with npm run dev to an app you can download.
body:
Four changes that take tscircuit desktop from "runs with `npm run dev`" to an app you can download.

## Automatic releases

A **Release** workflow builds the app for Apple Silicon on a macOS runner.

- Every push to `main` publishes a GitHub release with a `.dmg` and `.zip`, versioned `<major>.<minor>.<run number>` (major and minor from `package.json`). Documentation-only changes do not release.
- On a pull request that changes the workflow it only builds and keeps the zip as an artifact. That is how this PR's builds were made.

**The app does not update itself yet.** macOS only applies an update signed by the same developer, and these builds are not signed with an Apple Developer ID. Releases are therefore built without an update feed, so the app says updates are unavailable instead of downloading something it cannot install. The README section "Releases and automatic updates" lists the three things turning them on needs; the first is Apple signing secrets.

Unsigned also means macOS asks for confirmation on first open (Privacy & Security → Open Anyway). The workflow signs the bundle ad hoc so it is at least internally consistent; without that `codesign --verify` rejects what the build script produces.

## The tscircuit skill is bundled

`setup` downloads the newest [tscircuit/skill](https://github.com/tscircuit/skill) and packs it into the server, so each build carries the skill as of the day it was built. When the app starts it installs the skill to `~/.agents/skills/tscircuit` and `~/.claude/skills/tscircuit`.

It only replaces copies it installed itself (they carry a marker file). A folder of that name without the marker, such as one from `npx skills add`, is left alone.

## The app is called plain "tscircuit desktop"

T3 Code appends "(Beta)" or "(Nightly)" to the app's name. Both are gone; only `npm run dev` keeps "(Dev)".

## The icon fills the full square

The first icon used the tscircuit logo's own outline, which is narrower and rounder than the square macOS expects, so macOS drew it smaller than other apps' icons. It is now the logo's letters on a standard rounded square (`branding/app-icon.svg`).

That first logo came from `static/logo/ts.svg` in tscircuit/docs, which is missing the white pin 1 dot in the top left corner. `branding/icon.svg` is now a vector redrawing of https://tscircuit.com/tscircuit-logo.png, and the app icon and the in-app "ts" mark are made from it, dot included. tscircuit/docs#1024 corrects the docs file.

## Also

- **Export bug fixed.** A patch whose last context line was blank lost that line and no longer applied. CI caught it on this PR; there are now two tests for it.
- `check:app` also typechecks the server and desktop apps.

## Tested

- `npm test`: 18 script tests. `npm run check:app`: three typechecks, lint, 126 tests, unused-code check.
- The PR build with the new name and icon was installed on an Apple Silicon Mac.

## Not tested

- **The publish step.** It only runs on `main`, so the first real release happens when this merges.
- **The skill install on a real machine.** It is covered by four unit tests against a temporary folder, not yet by a run of the built app.
- **A downloaded `.dmg`.** The installed copy came from the zip, placed without the browser's quarantine flag, so the Gatekeeper prompt described above has not been seen first-hand.
